## Project layout

```
d:\Yggdrasil\
├── .clangd                        ← tells clangd to add -Iinclude (fixes IDE errors)
├── Makefile                       ← all/debug/release/test/clean targets
├── build.ps1                      ← PowerShell wrapper (Debug|Release|Clean|Test)
│
├── include/                       ← ALL headers
│   ├── token.h                    ← TokenKind enum + Token struct
│   ├── lexer.h                    ← Lexer class + LexMode enum
│   ├── ast.h                      ← NodeKind enum, Node struct, makeNode()
│   ├── parser.h                   ← Parser class + ParseError
│   ├── codegen.h                  ← CodeGen class
│   └── diagnostics.h              ← LexError, ParseError, CodeGenError, formatDiag()
│
├── src/                           ← ALL implementation files
│   ├── lexer.cpp
│   ├── parser.cpp
│   ├── codegen.cpp
│   └── main.cpp
│

```

## Build

```powershell
.\build.ps1                        # debug build → bin\yggdrasil.exe
.\build.ps1 -Mode Release
.\build.ps1 -Mode Test             # runs all fixtures
.\tests\runner\run_tests.ps1       # standalone runner with diff output
make                               # from Git Bash / WSL
make test
```

[436] [assistant_text] The parser is failing on `<input disabled />` — it's consuming `disabled` as the attribute name, then seeing `/` and expecting another attribute name instead of recognising `/>`. The JSX attribute loop needs to stop when it sees `/>`. Let me check the parser's attribute-scanning loop:
[438] [tool_result]  RESULT: 736:    while (!check(TokenKind::JSXGreater) && !check(TokenKind::JSXSlashGreater) && !atEnd()) {
[439] [assistant_text] The loop condition is correct. The real problem is the lexer: when in `JSXTag` mode, it sees `/` then `>` but the `/>` compound token (`JSXSlashGreater`) is only scanned if `/` is the *first* character peeked. But after emitting `disabled` as an `Identifier`, the lexer is still in `JSXTag` mode and should see `/>` — yet the parser never pushed `JSXTag` mode onto the lexer in the first place. The parser and lexer mode stacks are never connected: the parser has `inExpressionContext_` but never calls `lexer.pushMode()`. Since tokenisation is done eagerly upfront (all tokens produced before parsing starts), the mode stack on the lexer is irrelevant at parse time — but that means the lexer had no JSX context when it scanned the tokens, so it never emitted `JSXLess`, `JSXSlashGreater` etc.

The fix: the lexer's eager `tokenize()` needs to self-manage its own mode stack as it scans — driven by the tokens it sees, not by the parser. Let me rewrite the lexer to track JSX state internally:

34	char Lexer::advance() {
35	    char c = src_[pos_++];

41	void Lexer::skipWhitespaceAndComments() {
42	    while (!atEnd()) {
43	        char c = peek();
44	        if (std::isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(c))) {
45	            advance();
46	        } else if (c == '/' && peek(1) == '/') {
47	            while (!atEnd() && peek() != '\n') advance();
48	        } else if (c == '/' && peek(1) == '*') {
49	            advance(); advance(); // consume /*
50	            while (!atEnd() && !(peek() == '*' && peek(1) == '/'))
51	                advance();
52	            if (!atEnd()) { advance(); advance(); } // consume */
53	        } else {
54	            break;
55	        }
56	    }
57	}

106	Token Lexer::scanNumber() {
107	    int l = line_, c = col_;
108	    std::string v;
109	    // hex
110	    if (peek() == '0' && (peek(1) == 'x' || peek(1) == 'X')) {
111	        v += advance(); v += advance();
112	        while (!atEnd() && std::isxdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(peek())))
113	            v += advance();
114	        return makeToken(TokenKind::Number, v, l, c);
115	    }
116	    while (!atEnd() && std::isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(peek())))
117	        v += advance();
118	    if (!atEnd() && peek() == '.' && std::isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(peek(1)))) {
119	        v += advance();
120	        while (!atEnd() && std::isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(peek())))
121	            v += advance();
122	    }
123	    if (!atEnd() && (peek() == 'e' || peek() == 'E')) {
124	        v += advance();
125	        if (!atEnd() && (peek() == '+' || peek() == '-')) v += advance();
126	        while (!atEnd() && std::isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(peek())))
127	            v += advance();
128	    }
129	    return makeToken(TokenKind::Number, v, l, c);
130	}

132	Token Lexer::scanString(char quote) {
133	    int l = line_, c = col_;
134	    advance(); // opening quote
135	    std::string v;
136	    while (!atEnd() && peek() != quote) {
137	        if (peek() == '\\') { v += advance(); if (!atEnd()) v += advance(); }
138	        else                   v += advance();
139	    }
140	    if (atEnd()) throw LexError("Unterminated string literal", l, c);
141	    advance(); // closing quote
142	    return makeToken(TokenKind::String, v, l, c);
143	}
144	
145	Token Lexer::scanTemplate() {
146	    int l = line_, c = col_;
147	    advance(); // `
148	    std::string v;
149	    int depth = 0;
150	    while (!atEnd()) {
151	        char ch = peek();
152	        if (ch == '\\') { v += advance(); if (!atEnd()) v += advance(); }
153	        else if (ch == '$' && peek(1) == '{') {
154	            v += advance(); v += advance(); ++depth;
155	        } else if (ch == '}' && depth > 0) {
156	            v += advance(); --depth;
157	        } else if (ch == '`' && depth == 0) {
158	            advance(); break;
159	        } else {
160	            v += advance();
161	        }
162	    }
163	    return makeToken(TokenKind::TemplateString, v, l, c);
164	}
165	
166	Token Lexer::scanIdentifierOrKeyword() {
167	    int l = line_, c = col_;
168	    std::string v;
169	    while (!atEnd() && (std::isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(peek()))
170	                        || peek() == '_' || peek() == '$'))
171	        v += advance();
172	    TokenKind k = keywordKind(v);
173	    return makeToken(k, v, l, c);
174	}
175	
176	Token Lexer::scanRegex(int tline, int tcol) {
177	    std::string v = "/";
178	    bool inClass = false;
179	    while (!atEnd()) {
180	        char ch = peek();
181	        if (ch == '\\') { v += advance(); if (!atEnd()) v += advance(); continue; }
182	        if (ch == '[')  { inClass = true;  v += advance(); continue; }
183	        if (ch == ']')  { inClass = false; v += advance(); continue; }
184	        if (ch == '/' && !inClass) { v += advance(); break; }
185	        v += advance();
186	    }
187	    // flags
188	    while (!atEnd() && std::isalpha(static_cast<unsigned char>(peek())))
189	        v += advance();
190	    return makeToken(TokenKind::Regex, v, tline, tcol);
191	}

193	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
194	// Disambiguation helpers
195	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196	bool Lexer::regexAllowed() const {
197	    switch (lastKind_) {
198	        case TokenKind::RParen:
199	        case TokenKind::RBracket:
200	        case TokenKind::Identifier:
201	        case TokenKind::Number:
202	        case TokenKind::String:
203	        case TokenKind::TemplateString:
204	        case TokenKind::PlusPlus:
205	        case TokenKind::MinusMinus:
206	            return false;
207	        default:
208	            return true;
209	    }
210	}

212	// < starts JSX only after: return, (, =, ,, [, {, ternary :, ||, &&, arrow =>
213	bool Lexer::jsxAllowed() const {
214	    switch (lastKind_) {
215	        case TokenKind::KW_return:
216	        case TokenKind::LParen:
217	        case TokenKind::Equals:
218	        case TokenKind::Comma:
219	        case TokenKind::LBracket:
220	        case TokenKind::LBrace:
221	        case TokenKind::Colon:
222	        case TokenKind::PipePipe:
223	        case TokenKind::AmpAmp:
224	        case TokenKind::Arrow:
225	        case TokenKind::QuestionQuestion:
226	        case TokenKind::EndOfFile:
227	            return true;
228	        default:
229	            return false;
230	    }
231	}

233	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
234	// JSX scanners
235	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
236	Token Lexer::scanJSXText() {
237	    int l = line_, c = col_;
238	    std::string v;
239	    while (!atEnd() && peek() != '<' && peek() != '{')
240	        v += advance();
241	    return makeToken(TokenKind::JSXText, v, l, c);
242	}
243	
244	Token Lexer::scanJSXString(char quote) {
245	    int l = line_, c = col_;
246	    advance(); // opening quote
247	    std::string v;
248	    while (!atEnd() && peek() != quote) {
249	        if (peek() == '\\') { v += advance(); if (!atEnd()) v += advance(); }
250	        else                   v += advance();
251	    }
252	    if (atEnd()) throw LexError("Unterminated JSX attribute string", l, c);
253	    advance();
254	    return makeToken(TokenKind::JSXString, v, l, c);
255	}
256	
257	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
258	// Punctuation scanner (JS mode)
259	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
260	Token Lexer::scanPunctuation() {
261	    int l = line_, c = col_;
262	    char ch = advance();
263	
264	    auto make = [&](TokenKind k, std::string v) {
265	        return makeToken(k, std::move(v), l, c);
266	    };
267	
268	    switch (ch) {
269	        case '(': return make(TokenKind::LParen,     "(");
270	        case ')': return make(TokenKind::RParen,     ")");
271	        case '{': return make(TokenKind::LBrace,     "{");
272	        case '}': return make(TokenKind::RBrace,     "}");
273	        case '[': return make(TokenKind::LBracket,   "[");
274	        case ']': return make(TokenKind::RBracket,   "]");
275	        case ';': return make(TokenKind::Semicolon,  ";");
276	        case ':': return make(TokenKind::Colon,      ":");
277	        case ',': return make(TokenKind::Comma,      ",");
278	        case '~': return make(TokenKind::Tilde,      "~");
279	        case '^': return make(TokenKind::Caret,      "^");
280	        case '%': {
281	            if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::PercentEquals, "%="); }
282	            return make(TokenKind::Percent, "%");
283	        }
284	        case '?': {
285	            if (peek() == '?') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::QuestionQuestion, "??"); }
286	            return make(TokenKind::QuestionMark, "?");
287	        }
288	        case '.': {
289	            if (peek() == '.' && peek(1) == '.') {
290	                advance(); advance(); return make(TokenKind::DotDotDot, "...");
291	            }
292	            return make(TokenKind::Dot, ".");
293	        }
294	        case '=': {
295	            if (peek() == '>') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::Arrow, "=>"); }
296	            if (peek() == '=') {
297	                advance();
298	                if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::EqualsEqualsEquals, "==="); }
299	                return make(TokenKind::EqualsEquals, "==");
300	            }
301	            return make(TokenKind::Equals, "=");
302	        }
303	        case '!': {
304	            if (peek() == '=') {
305	                advance();
306	                if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::BangEqualsEquals, "!=="); }
307	                return make(TokenKind::BangEquals, "!=");
308	            }
309	            return make(TokenKind::Bang, "!");
310	        }
311	        case '<': {
312	            if (jsxAllowed()) return make(TokenKind::JSXLess, "<");
313	            if (peek() == '<') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::LShift, "<<"); }
314	            if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::LessEquals, "<="); }
315	            return make(TokenKind::Less, "<");
316	        }
317	        case '>': {
318	            if (peek() == '>') {
319	                advance();
320	                if (peek() == '>') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::URShift, ">>>"); }
321	                return make(TokenKind::RShift, ">>");
322	            }
323	            if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::GreaterEquals, ">="); }
324	            return make(TokenKind::Greater, ">");
325	        }
326	        case '+': {
327	            if (peek() == '+') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::PlusPlus, "++"); }
328	            if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::PlusEquals, "+="); }
329	            return make(TokenKind::Plus, "+");
330	        }
331	        case '-': {
332	            if (peek() == '-') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::MinusMinus, "--"); }
333	            if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::MinusEquals, "-="); }
334	            return make(TokenKind::Minus, "-");
335	        }
336	        case '*': {
337	            if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::StarEquals, "*="); }
338	            return make(TokenKind::Star, "*");
339	        }
340	        case '/': {
341	            if (regexAllowed()) return scanRegex(l, c);
342	            if (peek() == '=') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::SlashEquals, "/="); }
343	            return make(TokenKind::Slash, "/");
344	        }
345	        case '&': {
346	            if (peek() == '&') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::AmpAmp, "&&"); }
347	            return make(TokenKind::Amp, "&");
348	        }
349	        case '|': {
350	            if (peek() == '|') { advance(); return make(TokenKind::PipePipe, "||"); }
351	            return make(TokenKind::Pipe, "|");
352	        }
353	        default:
354	            return make(TokenKind::Unknown, std::string(1, ch));
355	    }
356	}
357	
358	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
359	// Main tokenise loop
360	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
361	std::vector<Token> Lexer::tokenize() {
362	    std::vector<Token> tokens;
363	
364	    while (true) {
365	        skipWhitespaceAndComments();
366	        if (atEnd()) {
367	            tokens.push_back(makeToken(TokenKind::EndOfFile, "", line_, col_));
368	            break;
369	        }
370	
371	        LexMode mode = currentMode();
372	        Token   tok;
373	
374	        if (mode == LexMode::JSXChildren) {
375	            char ch = peek();
376	            if (ch == '<') {
377	                int l = line_, c = col_;
378	                advance();
379	                if (peek() == '/') {
380	                    advance();
381	                    tok = makeToken(TokenKind::JSXLessSlash, "</", l, c);
382	                } else {
383	                    tok = makeToken(TokenKind::JSXLess, "<", l, c);
384	                }
385	            } else if (ch == '{') {
386	                int l = line_, c = col_;
387	                advance();
388	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::LBrace, "{", l, c);
389	                // Parser will pop JSXChildren and push JS for the expression,
390	                // then push JSXChildren again after }.
391	            } else {
392	                tok = scanJSXText();
393	            }
394	        } else if (mode == LexMode::JSXTag) {
395	            char ch = peek();
396	            if (ch == '/' && peek(1) == '>') {
397	                int l = line_, c = col_;
398	                advance(); advance();
399	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::JSXSlashGreater, "/>", l, c);
400	            } else if (ch == '>') {
401	                int l = line_, c = col_;
402	                advance();
403	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::JSXGreater, ">", l, c);
404	            } else if (ch == '{') {
405	                int l = line_, c = col_;
406	                advance();
407	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::LBrace, "{", l, c);
408	            } else if (ch == '"' || ch == '\'') {
409	                tok = scanJSXString(ch);
410	            } else if (std::isalpha(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) || ch == '_') {
411	                tok = scanIdentifierOrKeyword();
412	                tok.kind = TokenKind::Identifier; // tag/attr names aren't keywords in JSX
413	            } else if (ch == '.') {
414	                int l = line_, c = col_;
415	                advance();
416	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::Dot, ".", l, c);
417	            } else if (ch == '=') {
418	                int l = line_, c = col_;
419	                advance();
420	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::Equals, "=", l, c);
421	            } else if (ch == '.') {
422	                int l = line_, c = col_;
423	                advance();
424	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::Dot, ".", l, c);
425	            } else if (ch == '.' && peek(1) == '.' && peek(2) == '.') {
426	                int l = line_, c = col_;
427	                advance(); advance(); advance();
428	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::DotDotDot, "...", l, c);
429	            } else {
430	                // Fallback: identifiers, dots, equals already handled above.
431	                tok = makeToken(TokenKind::Unknown, std::string(1, advance()), line_, col_);
432	            }
433	        } else {
434	            // Normal JS mode
435	            char ch = peek();
436	            if (std::isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch))) {
437	                tok = scanNumber();
438	            } else if (ch == '"' || ch == '\'') {
439	                tok = scanString(ch);
440	            } else if (ch == '`') {
441	                tok = scanTemplate();
442	            } else if (std::isalpha(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) || ch == '_' || ch == '$') {
443	                tok = scanIdentifierOrKeyword();
444	            } else {
445	                tok = scanPunctuation();
446	            }
447	        }
448	
449	        lastKind_ = tok.kind;
450	        tokens.push_back(std::move(tok));
451	    }
452	
453	    return tokens;
454	}

364	//   JSXGreater emitted (tag)   -> pop JSXTag, push JSXChildren
365	//   JSXSlashGreater emitted    -> pop JSXTag          (self-closing)

367	//   JSXGreater emitted (close) -> pop JSXTag          (closing tag done)
368	//   LBrace in JSXChildren      -> push JS

1. Token 75 `>` at col 43 — that's `JSXGreater` correctly emitted after `}`. Good.

But wait — `>` at col 43 is kind 75. Let me check: `JSXGreater` is kind 81, `Greater` is kind 75. So the `>` after `}` was emitted as a plain JS `Greater` token, not `JSXGreater`. That means when `}` was processed in the JS-inside-JSXTag context, the pop went back to JS mode instead of JSXTag. The `jsxBraceDepth` pop returned to JSXChildren (the wrong parent) or the mode was wrong.

The issue: the `{` for a JSX attribute expression is in `JSXTag` mode. When we push JS for the expression and then pop back after `}`, we pop back to `JSXTag` — but then the `>` check runs in the JS branch (bottom of the loop), not the JSXTag branch, because `currentMode()` returned to JSXTag *after* the RBrace was already processed in the JS branch with `continue`. Then the next iteration should pick up `>` in JSXTag mode. Let me re-check...

Actually the token dump shows `}` at col 42 (kind 38 = `RBrace`) and `>` at col 43 (kind 75 = `Greater`). The `}` consumed the JSX brace depth and popped back to JSXTag — correct. But then on the next iteration the mode should be JSXTag and `>` should emit `JSXGreater` (kind 81). It's emitting kind 75 instead, meaning it went through the JS `scanPunctuation()` path. So either the pop didn't work or `jsxBraceDepth` tracking is wrong for attributes (JSXTag context, not JSXChildren).

The bug: `jsxBraceDepth` is pushed in JSXTag `{` handler, but the JS `}` handler only pops when `braceDepth == jsxBraceDepth.back() + 1`. The attribute `{` advances braceDepth to 1 inside JS mode — wait, no. The `{` in JSXTag pushes JS mode *before* the brace depth tracking in the JS branch runs. When `{` of `{()=>...}` is seen in JSXTag: we emit LBrace, push `jsxBraceDepth.back() = braceDepth = 0`, push JS mode. Then in JS mode, `(`, `)`, `=>`, `count`, `+`, `1` are all scanned. `braceDepth` is still 0 throughout (no `{` or `}` seen in JS yet). Then `}` is seen: `braceDepth == 0` and `jsxBraceDepth.back() + 1 == 1` — condition `braceDepth == jsxBraceDepth.back() + 1` is `0 == 1` — **false**. So it falls through to `--braceDepth` making it -1, and does NOT pop the mode. That's the bug — the condition is off by one.

The `{` in JSXTag mode never incremented `braceDepth` (it was handled before entering JS mode). So when we enter JS, `braceDepth` is still 0 and the closing `}` should trigger when `braceDepth == 0` and there's a pending jsxBraceDepth entry. Fix the condition:

[786] [assistant_text] The issue: when stderr output from a native exe is redirected via `2>&1` in PS 5.1, each stderr line becomes an `ErrorRecord`. The `try/catch` catches the exception thrown by the ErrorRecord, but `$LASTEXITCODE` is only set to the actual process exit code after the process completes — but in PS 5.1, a caught `NativeCommandError` resets `$LASTEXITCODE` to the internal error code (-1). The fix: don't redirect stderr at all for exit-code tests, just suppress the output:

[794] [user_text] time for stage 2/II

MVP Stage 2 — "Solid Tool"
After your basic transpiler works on single files, Stage 2 is about making it robust, usable, and fast without turning it into Babel.
1. Error Recovery & Diagnostics

    Don't crash on first error — resynchronize and report multiple errors per file
    Track source locations in AST nodes (line/column) for precise error pointing even without source maps
    Contextual error messages — "Expected > but found } — did you forget to close an attribute?"

2. Complete JSX Spec Coverage

    Member expression tags: <My.Component />, <context.Provider />
    Namespace tags: <svg:circle /> (if you care about SVG/mathML)
    Spread children: {...items} (rare but valid)
    Whitespace normalization in JSXText — collapse rules differ from HTML
    Comments inside JSX: {/* this */} properly stripped or preserved
    Boolean attributes: <input disabled /> → disabled: true

3. Configurable Output (via config.json or cmdline args)

    Pragma switching: React.createElement vs h() (Preact) vs _jsx (React 17+ automatic runtime)
    Development vs production flags: __source and __self props for React dev warnings
    JSX runtime import injection (React 17+ style: import { jsx } from 'react/jsx-runtime')

4. Performance & Architecture

    Arena allocator for AST nodes instead of individual new/delete or heavy smart pointer churn
    Zero-copy lexer — slice strings from source buffer instead of allocating
    Streaming/batch mode — transpile entire directories, not just stdin/single file
    CLI with flags: --pragma, --out-dir, --watch

5. Edge Case Hardening

    Unicode identifiers in tag names and attributes
    Complex expressions in attributes: <div attr={foo.bar[baz]()} />
    Nested ternaries with JSX: cond ? <A /> : <B /> (parser precedence handling)
    Adjacent JSX elements in expressions: (<></>) fragments wrapping siblings

Stage 2 Time Estimate
+2–3 weeks on top of MVP.

13	.PARAMETER Filter
14	    Optional glob filter on fixture base names, e.g. "01_*" or "err_*".
15	#>

17	    [string]$Binary = "",
18	    [string]$Filter = "*"
19	)
20	
21	Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
22	$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
23	
24	$RepoRoot    = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..") | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path
25	$FixturesDir = Join-Path $RepoRoot "tests\fixtures"
26	
27	if ($Binary -eq "") {
28	    $Binary = Join-Path $RepoRoot "bin\yggdrasil.exe"
29	}

32	    Write-Error "Binary not found: $Binary`nBuild first with: .\build.ps1"
33	}

35	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
36	# ANSI colour helpers
37	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
38	function Green  { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Green  -NoNewline }
39	function Red    { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Red    -NoNewline }
40	function Yellow { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Yellow -NoNewline }
41	function Cyan   { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Cyan   -NoNewline }
42	function Nl     { Write-Host "" }
43	
44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	# Diff helper — show first divergence
46	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
47	function Show-Diff {
48	    param([string]$Expected, [string]$Actual)
49	    $expLines = $Expected -split "`n"
50	    $actLines = $Actual   -split "`n"
51	    $max = [Math]::Max($expLines.Count, $actLines.Count)
52	    $shown = 0
53	    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $max -and $shown -lt 8; $i++) {
54	        $e = if ($i -lt $expLines.Count) { $expLines[$i] } else { "<missing>" }
55	        $a = if ($i -lt $actLines.Count) { $actLines[$i] } else { "<missing>" }
56	        if ($e -ne $a) {
57	            Yellow "    line $($i+1):`n"; Nl
58	            Green  "      expected: $e"; Nl
59	            Red    "      actual  : $a"; Nl
60	            $shown++
61	        }
62	    }
63	}
64	
65	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	# Collect fixtures
67	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68	$jsxFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $FixturesDir -Filter "$Filter.jsx" |
69	            Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch "^err_" -or $_.Name -match "^err_" } |
70	            Sort-Object Name
71	
72	$pass = 0
73	$fail = 0
74	$skip = 0
75	
76	Write-Host ""
77	Cyan "=== Yggdrasil Fixture Tests ==="; Nl
78	Write-Host "  Binary  : $Binary"
79	Write-Host "  Fixtures: $FixturesDir"
80	Write-Host "  Filter  : $Filter"
81	Write-Host ""
82	
83	foreach ($jsx in $jsxFiles) {
84	    $base        = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($jsx.FullName)
85	    $expectedJs  = Join-Path $FixturesDir "$base.expected.js"
86	    $expectedExit= Join-Path $FixturesDir "$base.expected_exit"
87	
88	    # ---- Error-exit test ----
89	    if (Test-Path $expectedExit) {
90	        $wantExit = (Get-Content $expectedExit -Raw).Trim()
91	        # Redirect stdout+stderr to null so PS 5.1 doesn't wrap stderr lines
92	        # in ErrorRecords (which corrupt $LASTEXITCODE via NativeCommandError).
93	        $null = cmd /c "`"$Binary`" `"$($jsx.FullName)`"" "2>nul"
94	        $gotExit  = $LASTEXITCODE
95	        if ([string]$gotExit -eq $wantExit) {
96	            Green "  PASS"; Write-Host " [exit=$gotExit] $($jsx.Name)"
97	            $pass++
98	        } else {
99	            Red   "  FAIL"; Write-Host " [exit=$gotExit, want=$wantExit] $($jsx.Name)"
100	            $fail++
101	        }
102	        continue
103	    }
104	
105	    # ---- Output comparison test ----
106	    if (-not (Test-Path $expectedJs)) {
107	        Yellow "  SKIP"; Write-Host " (no .expected.js) $($jsx.Name)"
108	        $skip++
109	        continue
110	    }
111	
112	    $expected = (Get-Content $expectedJs -Raw).Replace("`r`n", "`n").TrimEnd()
113	    try   { $actual = (& $Binary $jsx.FullName 2>&1 | Out-String).Replace("`r`n", "`n").TrimEnd() }
114	    catch { $actual = ($_.ToString()).Replace("`r`n", "`n").TrimEnd() }
115	    $exitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
116	
117	    if ($exitCode -ne 0) {
118	        Red   "  FAIL"; Write-Host " [exit=$exitCode] $($jsx.Name)"
119	        Write-Host "    stderr: $actual"
120	        $fail++
121	        continue
122	    }
123	
124	    if ($actual -eq $expected) {
125	        Green "  PASS"; Write-Host " $($jsx.Name)"
126	        $pass++
127	    } else {
128	        Red   "  FAIL"; Write-Host " $($jsx.Name)"
129	        Show-Diff $expected $actual
130	        $fail++
131	    }
132	}
133	
134	Write-Host ""
135	Cyan "Results: "; Nl
136	Green  "  $pass passed"; Nl
137	if ($fail -gt 0)  { Red    "  $fail failed"; Nl }
138	if ($skip -gt 0)  { Yellow "  $skip skipped"; Nl }
139	Write-Host ""
140	
141	if ($fail -gt 0) { exit 1 } else { exit 0 }

Yggdrasil — Stage 3 Summary
Directory CLI & Batch Transpiler
What It Is
Yggdrasil shifts from single-file stdin/stdout to a directory-aware CLI tool. Point it at a source folder, get transpiled JS in a dist/ mirror. No module resolution, no bundling — still just a transpiler.
Core Features
Table
Feature	Description
Recursive directory scan	src/ → dist/ tree mirroring via std::filesystem
Batch transpilation	All .jsx files processed in parallel (thread pool)
Passthrough mode	Plain .js files copied untouched (optional --no-copy)
Watch mode	Re-transpile changed files on save (polling or OS-native watcher)
Extension rewrite	.jsx → .js in output; directory structure preserved
CLI Interface
plain
Copy

yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --watch
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --jsx-pragma h --no-copy --verbose

Table
Flag	Behavior
--out-dir <path>	Required for batch mode
--watch	Monitor source and re-transpile deltas
--jsx-pragma <name>	Override React.createElement
--jsx-runtime <classic|automatic>	React 17+ _jsx runtime vs classic
--no-copy	Skip non-JSX .js files
--verbose	Print src/components/Button.jsx → dist/components/Button.js
What Yggdrasil Stage 3 Does NOT Do

    ❌ Parse or resolve import/export
    ❌ Touch node_modules
    ❌ Build dependency graphs
    ❌ Bundle, concatenate, or tree-shake
    ❌ Handle CSS, assets, or non-JS files beyond copy/passthrough
    ❌ Source maps (already excluded by design)

C++ Implementation Notes

    std::filesystem::recursive_directory_iterator for scanning
    Thread pool (std::thread + std::queue + mutex) for parallel file processing
    Watch mode: simple polling loop (cross-platform) or OS-specific APIs (inotify/FSEvents/ReadDirectoryChangesW) for efficiency
    Error isolation: one file failing doesn't kill the batch; aggregate error report at end

Output Example
plain
Copy

src/
  components/
    Button.jsx      →  dist/components/Button.js
    Icon.jsx        →  dist/components/Icon.js
  pages/
    Home.jsx        →  dist/pages/Home.js
  utils/
    helpers.js      →  dist/utils/helpers.js   (copied)

[1301] [assistant_text] I see two issues:
1. `import Button from "../components/Button"` (default import) is being emitted as `import { Button }` — default imports need special handling. Let me check the import parser.

The import parser for `import Default from "mod"` — it stores it as a specifier with just `name` set. But `genImportDecl` only handles `*` or named `{ }`. Default imports get emitted as `{ Button }`. Let me fix `genImportDecl`:
[1303] [tool_result]  RESULT: 108	}
109	
110	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
111	// Statements
112	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
113	void CodeGen::genImportDecl(const Node& n) {
114	    emit("import ");
115	    if (n.specifiers.empty()) {
116	        // side-effect import
117	    } else if (n.specifiers.size() == 1 && n.specifiers[0]->name == "*") {
118	        emit("* as " + n.specifiers[0]->value);
119	    } else {
120	        bool first = true;
121	        emit("{ ");
122	        for (const auto& s : n.specifiers) {
123	            if (!first) emit(", ");
124	            first = false;
125	            emit(s->name);
126	            if (!s->value.empty()) emit(" as " + s->value);
127	        }
128	        emit(" }");
129	    }
130	    if (!n.source.empty()) emit(" from \"" + n.source + "\"");

### Bug fixed during Stage 3
**Default import codegen** — `import Button from "./Button"` was incorrectly emitted as `import { Button } from "./Button"`. Fixed by tagging default-import specifiers with `boolVal = true` in the parser and separating them from named specifiers in `genImportDecl`.

Let me compute the actual `ChoicePoint` size:

- `candidates[320]` = 320 × 4 = 1280 bytes
- `cand_count` + `cand_idx` = 8 bytes  
- `goal` + `trail_mark` + `goal_top` = 12 bytes
- Total ≈ 1300 bytes
- `ChoiceStack` = 256 × 1300 = 332KB

In `try_clause`:
```cpp
static RenameMap rm;
memset(&rm, 0, sizeof(RenameMap));

```

`mark` is the trail state **before** the rename+unify attempt. If unify fails, we call `trail_undo(&env->trail, env->vars, mark)` which undoes back to pre-rename state. Good.

But in the backtrack loop:
```cpp
trail_undo(&env->trail, env->vars, cp->trail_mark);
```

`cp->trail_mark` is the trail state when the choice point was created. When we first enter backtrack for a choice point that was just pushed (for `path(a,b)`/`path(a,c)`) — the trail_mark was set before the FIRST candidate was tried. But `try_clause` for the first candidate already undid to its own mark on failure. So `cp->trail_mark` and the current trail state are both at the pre-candidate position. `trail_undo` to `cp->trail_mark` is a no-op.

Wait — looking at the forward section again:
```cpp

cp->goal_top   = gs.top;
...

    goto backtrack;

```

The `trail_mark` is taken BEFORE `try_clause`. `try_clause` creates its own internal mark. If `try_clause` fails, it calls `trail_undo(env->trail, env->vars, mark)` where `mark` = trail state at entry to `try_clause`. So after a failed `try_clause`, the trail is at the same state as when `cp->trail_mark` was set. 

Now in the forward section when `try_clause` **succeeds** for `reachable/2`:
- Trail advances (binding `fresh_X=a`, `fresh_Y=c`)
- Body goal `path(fresh_X, fresh_Y)` = `path(a, c)` pushed
- Forward to next iteration
- Pop `path(a,c)`, look up `path/2`, get candidates [path(a,b), path(a,c)]
- `cp2->trail_mark = trail_mark(trail)` ← this is AFTER the `reachable` bindings
- Try `path(a,b)` → fails → trail undone to `cp2->trail_mark`
- Backtrack: `trail_undo(env->trail, vars, cp2->trail_mark)` ← same state, no-op
- Try `path(a,c)` → succeeds!
- `cs.top` decremented (it was the last candidate)
- `goto next_iter` → continue

Let me add a targeted debug print to understand what's happening — actually, let me check if this is a static-scope issue with the query result callback. Looking at `test_solver.cpp` line 85-88:

The `solve` function returns the number of solutions. If it returns 0 for `reachable(a, c)`, it means either the goal failed or the index is returning wrong candidates.

Let me check if the issue might be in the static `clause_vars` being reset between clause loads but the variables from previous loads still being in the static `clause_arena`. The `rename_term` function copies from `clause_arena` into `query_arena`. If `clause_vars` was reset but `clause_arena` contains variables from old clause loads...

Actually `clause_vars` is re-init'd in `load()`: `var_registry_init(&clause_vars)`. This clears all variable registrations. But the term nodes in `clause_arena` still reference old `VarId`s. After reset, `var_alloc` starts from index 1 again, potentially creating a new variable with the same `VarId` as an old one.

This is the key bug: `var_registry_init` resets the count to 0, so the next `var_alloc` returns `VarId=1`. But a previously stored term in `clause_arena` also references `VarId=1` (from a previous load). When `rename_term` copies that term and calls `var_alloc` on `env->vars`, it creates a fresh var with ID `n` in the query's `VarRegistry`, which is correct. But the issue is that **two different logical variables from different clauses share the same `VarId` in clause_vars**, so when renamed into the query arena, they might collide in the `RenameMap`.

Wait — `rename_term` creates new `VarId`s in `env->vars` (the query vars), not in `clause_vars`. And it uses the `RenameMap` to ensure that within a single clause rename, the same old `VarId` maps to the same fresh `VarId`. But the old `VarId`s in the **same** clause are all unique (since they were allocated sequentially within `clause_vars` before it was reset). The problem would only arise if two clauses were renamed simultaneously sharing the same `RenameMap`, but that doesn't happen.

The real issue is that after `var_registry_init(&clause_vars)`, the VarId counter resets to 0. The next load will allocate `VarId=1, 2, 3...` again. Two clauses loaded in different `load()` calls with an intervening `var_registry_init` will have their variables with overlapping `VarId`s (both use 1, 2, 3...). When `rename_term` processes clause 1 (VarId=1 → fresh1) and then clause 2 (VarId=1 → fresh2?), the `RenameMap` is cleared per clause, so no collision.

// Patched solve that prints each step
static AtomTable   g_atoms;

const char *atom_name(AtomId id) {
    return atom_spelling(&g_atoms, id);
}

void print_term(TermRef ref, const TermArena *arena, const VarRegistry *vars, int depth = 0) {
    if (depth > 5 || ref == TERM_REF_INVALID) { printf("?"); return; }
    TermRef dr = deref(ref, arena, vars);
    const Term *t = term_get(arena, dr);
    if (!t) { printf("NULL"); return; }
    switch (t->kind) {
        case TERM_KIND_ATOM: printf("%s", atom_name(t->data.atom_id)); break;
        case TERM_KIND_INT:  printf("%d", t->data.int_val); break;
        case TERM_KIND_VAR:  printf("_%u", t->data.var.var_id); break;
        case TERM_KIND_COMPOUND:
            printf("%s(", atom_name(t->data.compound.functor));
            for (uint8_t i = 0; i < t->data.compound.arity; i++) {
                if (i) printf(",");
                print_term(term_arg(arena, dr, i), arena, vars, depth+1);
            }
            printf(")");
            break;
        default: printf("?kind");
    }
}

    static VarRegistry query_vars;

        if (r == PARSE_EOF) break;
        if (r != PARSE_OK) { printf("PARSE ERR\n"); break; }
        db_assert_last(&db, &c, &clause_arena);

        for (uint32_t si = 0; si < pp->index.idx_count[bi]; si++) {
            uint32_t pos = pp->index.idx_clause_slots[pp->index.idx_start[bi] + si];
            const StoredClause *sc = db_get_clause(&db, pos);

And bucket 1 (`b`):
- `slot[0]=pos1 head=path(b,c)` ← correct, but start=1 instead of start=2

The bug is in `db_build_index`: buckets are built contiguously in `idx_clause_slots`, but when bucket `b` is created **after** bucket `a` already has 1 entry, bucket `b`'s start is set to `idx_slot_count = 1`. But the `path(a,c)` clause (ci=2) comes after `path(b,c)` (ci=1), so when ci=2 hits bucket `a`, it appends to `idx_clause_slots[2]`, but bucket `b`'s start=1, count=1, which now overlaps with bucket `a`'s second slot.

The issue: **buckets don't stay contiguous** when multiple buckets interleave. I assumed clauses for the same functor/first-arg come consecutively (e.g., all `a` clauses first, then all `b` clauses), but they're interleaved (`a,b`, `b,c`, `a,c`).

I need to fix the index build to use a two-pass approach: first count per bucket, allocate slot ranges, then fill in:

[262] [assistant_text] `test_solver` now passes 22/22. `test_indexing` still stack overflows. The test itself uses `IdxCtx` structs with local (non-static) members. Let me check what's large in the test:

The `IdxCtx` struct has:
- `AtomTable atoms` = 4096 × 260 bytes ≈ 1MB
- `Database db` = `4096 × ~1320 bytes` (StoredClause) + `512 × PredEntry(huge)` 

The `PredEntry` now contains a `FirstArgIndex` which has `BucketTemp`-like fields:
- `idx_clause_slots[256]` = 1KB
- `idx_var_slots[64]` = 256 bytes
- etc.

`Database` = 4096 clauses × ~1320 bytes + 512 predicates × sizeof(PredEntry).

Let me check `sizeof(PredEntry)`:

`FirstArgIndex`:
- `idx_key[64]` = 64 × 4 = 256 bytes
- `idx_kind[64]` = 64 bytes  
- `idx_start[64]` + `idx_count[64]` = 512 bytes
- `idx_clause_slots[256]` = 1KB
- `idx_slot_count` = 4 bytes
- `idx_var_slots[64]` = 256 bytes
- `idx_var_count` + `built` = ~8 bytes
- Total FirstArgIndex ≈ **2.1KB**

`PredEntry` = functor + arity + first + count + `FirstArgIndex` ≈ **2.1KB**

`Database` = `StoredClause clauses[4096]` + `PredEntry preds[512]` 

`StoredClause` size: `head(4) + body[32×4=128] + body_len(4) + id(4)` = **136 bytes**

`Database` = `4096 × 136 + 512 × ~2100` ≈ `557KB + 1075KB` ≈ **1.6MB**

And `IdxCtx` has TWO `TermArena`s. Each `TermArena` = 8192 × `sizeof(Term)` + `ArgPool`.

`Term` size ≈ 4 (kind) + max(4,4,12,4) (union) + 4 (ref) + padding = ~24 bytes.
`TermArena` = 8192 × 24 + 4 + 32768 × 4 + 4 ≈ **328KB**.

`IdxCtx` total ≈ `AtomTable(1MB) + Database(1.6MB) + 2 × TermArena(328KB each) + 2 × VarRegistry(1024 × ~80bytes = 82KB each)` ≈ **3.4MB**.

With `IdxCtx` as a local variable on the stack in each test case, and ~12 test cases, the test framework's `run_all()` calls them sequentially (no nesting), so only one is on the stack at a time. But the 3.4MB still exceeds the default Windows stack size (1MB).

The fix: make `IdxCtx` members static in the test, similar to how `test_solver.cpp` does it:

9	
10	Epilog is a greenfield logic programming runtime. The tagline: "not Prolog rewritten, but the next evolutionary step after Prolog."
11	
12	**Why:** Prolog was designed for single-core, limited-memory systems. Epilog targets modern hardware — multicore CPUs, large datasets, database-backed facts, and speculative/predictive inference.
13	
14	**How to apply:** All work starts at v0.1 (minimal Prolog-compatible runtime). Features like prediction, multicore, and database integration come later. Never let optimization or speculation layers influence logical correctness.
15	
16	## Version milestones
17	- 0.1: Facts, rules, unification, backtracking, query execution, REPL
18	- 0.2: Indexing, caching, query statistics
19	- 0.3: Reactive reasoning / dependency graph (the "Reasoning DOM")
20	- 0.4: SQLite / database-backed facts
21	- 0.5: Neo4j / graph reasoning
22	- 0.6: Predictive execution (speculative cache)
23	- 0.7: Multicore parallel inference
24	- 1.0: Stable release
25	
26	## Key architectural invariant
27	The inference engine is the source of truth. Predictions/cache/speculation affect speed only — never facts, rules, or conclusions.
28

2	
3	> *The next evolutionary step after Prolog.*
4	
5	Epilog is a logic programming runtime written in **C++23**, inspired by Prolog and designed from the ground up for modern hardware: multicore CPUs, incremental reasoning, predictive execution, and database-backed fact storage.
6	
7	It is not a Prolog rewrite. It is what comes after.

11	## Status
12	
13	**Version 0.1 — Minimal Prolog Runtime** (current)
14	
15	A working interactive REPL with facts, rules, unification, backtracking, and a core set of built-in predicates. The foundation everything else is built on.
16

19	## Quick Start
20	
21	### Build
22	
23	**Windows:**
24	```bat
25	build.bat
26	```
27	
28	**Linux / macOS:**
29	```sh
30	bash build.sh
31	```
32	
33	**Make:**
34	```sh
35	make          # release build  (-O2)
36	make debug    # debug build    (-g -O0)
37	```
38	
39	Requires `clang++` 21+ with C++23 support. Falls back to `clang-cl` on Windows if `clang++` fails.
40	
41	### Run
42	
43	**Interactive REPL:**
44	```bat
45	run.bat
46	```
47	```sh
48	bash run.sh
49	```
50	or directly:
51	```sh
52	./epilog
53	```
54	
55	**Load a file then start the REPL:**
56	```sh
57	./epilog facts.pl
58	```
59	
60	**Verbose / debug tracing:**
61	```sh
62	./epilog --verbose
63	./epilog -v facts.pl
64	```
65	Logs every resolution step, clause lookup, and unification result to stderr.
66

68	
69	## The Language (Prolog subset)
70	
71	### Facts
72	
73	```prolog
74	parent(alice, bob).
75	parent(bob, carol).
76	```
77	
78	### Rules
79	
80	```prolog
81	grandparent(X, Y) :-
82	    parent(X, Z),
83	    parent(Z, Y).
84	```
85	
86	### Queries
87	
88	```prolog
89	?- grandparent(alice, carol).
90	```
91	```
92	true ;
93	```
94	
95	```prolog
96	?- parent(X, Y).
97	```
98	```
99	X = alice
100	Y = bob ;
101	```
102	
103	### Loading a file
104	
105	From the REPL:
106	```prolog
107	consult('my_facts.pl').
108	```
109	
110	Or on startup:
111	```sh
112	./epilog my_facts.pl
113	```
114	
115	### Exiting
116	
117	```prolog
118	halt.
119	```
120

123	## Built-in Predicates (v0.1)
124	
125	| Predicate | Description |
126	|-----------|-------------|
127	| `true/0` | Always succeeds |
128	| `fail/0` | Always fails |
129	| `false/0` | Alias for `fail/0` |
130	| `!/0` | Cut — discard remaining choice points |
131	| `=/2` | Unification: `X = Y` |
132	| `\=/2` | Non-unification: succeeds if `X` and `Y` cannot unify |
133	| `write/1` | Print a term to stdout |
134	| `nl/0` | Print a newline |
135	| `assert/1` | Add a clause to the database (assertz semantics) |
136	| `assertz/1` | Alias for `assert/1` |
137	| `retract/1` | Remove the first matching clause |

141	## Architecture
142	
143	```
144	epilog/
145	├── include/           Headers (.hpp) — shared across all layers
146	│   ├── atoms.hpp      Atom interning table
147	│   ├── variables.hpp  Logic variable registry + TermRef/VarId typedefs
148	│   ├── terms.hpp      Term representation (atom, var, int, compound)
149	│   ├── lexer.hpp      Tokenizer
150	│   ├── parser.hpp     Clause and query parser
151	│   ├── database.hpp   Clause store
152	│   ├── unifier.hpp    Robinson unification + Trail
153	│   ├── solver.hpp     Backtracking SLD resolution engine
154	│   ├── builtins.hpp   Built-in predicate dispatch
155	│   ├── repl.hpp       Read-Eval-Print Loop
156	│   └── log.hpp        Verbose logging (--verbose flag)
157	│
158	├── internals/         Core data structures
159	│   ├── atoms.cpp      FNV-1a hash table, open addressing, O(1) lookup
160	│   ├── variables.cpp  Per-query variable registry with Trail undo
161	│   └── terms.cpp      Arena allocator — no malloc after init
162	│
163	├── parser/            Language frontend
164	│   ├── lexer.cpp      Single-pass tokenizer, no backtracking
165	│   └── parser.cpp     Iterative top-down parser, no C recursion
166	│
167	├── engine/            Inference backend
168	│   ├── database.cpp   Predicate-indexed clause store
169	│   ├── unifier.cpp    Iterative unification with explicit work stack
170	│   ├── solver.cpp     Goal stack + choice-point stack, no C recursion
171	│   └── builtins.cpp   Dispatch table for built-in predicates
172	│
173	├── repl.cpp           Interactive REPL, file loader
174	└── main.cpp           Entry point, CLI argument handling
175	```
176	
177	### Key Design Decisions
178	
179	**C++23, not C.**
180	The codebase was originally C11 and converted to C++23. Benefits: `constexpr` constants instead of `#define`, `nullptr` instead of `NULL`, `static_cast` instead of C casts, scoped enums, aggregate initialisation, and `bool` instead of `int` for predicate returns. The JPL safety constraints (no post-init heap, bounded loops, no C-stack recursion) are retained.
181	
182	**No heap allocation after init.**
183	Every subsystem uses a fixed-size arena or table declared at startup. `new`/`malloc` are never called during query execution. This follows JPL Rule 3 and makes memory behaviour fully predictable.
184	
185	**No C-stack recursion in the engine.**
186	The unifier uses an explicit `UnifyPair` work stack. The solver uses an explicit `GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack`. `rename_term` recurses only over compound arity (bounded by `TERM_MAX_ARITY = 255`). This follows JPL Rule 1.
187	
188	**Separate arenas for clauses and queries.**
189	Clause terms (asserted facts and rules) live in a persistent `clause_arena`. Each query gets its own `query_arena` that is reset between queries. Stored `TermRef` indices into `clause_arena` remain stable across queries.
190	
191	**Variable names stored in Term nodes.**
192	Each `TERM_KIND_VAR` node carries its source-level name (`char name[64]`). The solver reads names directly from clause-arena term nodes when creating fresh renamed variables for each clause application — no dependency on a stale variable registry.
193	
194	**`TermRef` bindings via `TERM_TERMREF` tag.**
195	Variables are bound to `TermRef` indices (into the query arena) rather than splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## JPL Coding Standard Compliance
200	
201	All source files follow the [NASA/JPL Institutional Coding Standard](https://yurichev.com/mirrors/C/JPL_Coding_Standard_C.pdf):
202	
203	| Rule | How it is applied |
204	|------|------------------|
205	| **1** — No goto\*, no recursion | Engine uses explicit `GoalStack`/`ChoiceStack`; unifier uses a `UnifyPair` work stack |
206	| **2** — Fixed loop bounds | Every loop is bounded by a named `constexpr` capacity constant |
207	| **3** — No post-init dynamic allocation | All storage is pre-declared in fixed-size structs; no `new`/`malloc` during inference |
208	| **4** — Short functions | No function exceeds ~60 lines |
209	| **5** — Check all parameters and return values | Every public function validates inputs; callers check return codes |
210	| **6** — Preprocessor for includes and constants only | All constants are `constexpr`; no token pasting |
211	| **7** — Pointer depth ≤ 1 | No `**` in public APIs; all access through flat index types (`TermRef`, `VarId`, `AtomId`) |
212	| **8** — All warnings enabled | Built with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` |
213	
214	\* `goto` is used in `solver.cpp` for the backtracking label — it does not jump across any variable initialisations, satisfying C++ legality. The alternatives (recursive lambda, exception, setjmp) are worse under JPL rules.

[433] [user_text] Time for Stage 3,
FrostCore Stage 3 — "Parser/Bytecode Boundary"
After memory and stdlib are modular, the next cut is separating the frontend from the backend. quickjs-ng's parser emits bytecode directly into runtime-specific structures. Stage 3 makes the parser a standalone compilation unit that produces a portable intermediate representation the VM can load independently.
Core Tasks
Table
#	Task	What It Means
1	Extract parser state	Remove parser's hidden dependency on JSRuntime internals. Parser should only need: source string, allocator, error callback.
2	Bytecode container	Define frost_bytecode struct — a self-contained blob of opcodes, constants, atom table, and function tables. No runtime pointers.
3	Parse interface	frost_parse(const char* source, frost_bytecode** out, frost_error* err) — source in, bytecode out.
4	Load interface	frost_runtime_load(rt, frost_bytecode* bc) — VM ingests pre-parsed bytecode. Enables parse-once, run-many.
5	Atom table isolation	Parser builds its own atom table during parse. Runtime merges it on load. Breaks the current global atom table assumption.
6	Compilation unit split	Physical separation: frost_parse.c (lexer + parser), frost_bytecode.c (IR format), frost_vm.c (execution engine).
Deliverables
plain
Copy
src/
  frost_alloc.c       // Stage 1
  frost_runtime.c     // Stage 1
  frost_std_*.c       // Stage 2
  frost_parse.c       // Stage 3 (NEW)
  frost_bytecode.c    // Stage 3 (NEW)
  frost_vm.c          // Stage 3 (split from monolith)
include/
  frostcore.h         // Updated with parse/load API
  frost_bytecode.h    // Bytecode IR definition (opaque to GlacioJS)
The API Surface (Stage 3)
c
Copy
// Opaque handle to compiled bytecode
typedef struct frost_bytecode frost_bytecode;

// Parse source into portable bytecode (no runtime needed)
int frost_parse(const char* source, frost_bytecode** out, frost_error* err);

// Load bytecode into a specific runtime for execution
int frost_runtime_load(frost_runtime* rt, frost_bytecode* bc);

// Execute already-loaded bytecode
int frost_runtime_eval_loaded(frost_runtime* rt, frost_bytecode* bc, JSValue* out);

// Destroy bytecode independently of runtime lifecycle
void frost_bytecode_destroy(frost_bytecode* bc);
Explicitly NOT in Stage 3
❌ C++ wrapper or AST exposure (bytecode is the boundary, not AST nodes)
❌ JIT compilation or codegen changes
❌ ES module resolution or loader hooks
❌ GC algorithm changes
❌ Multi-threaded parsing (single-threaded only)
❌ Isolate/task scheduler (still GlacioJS Layer 2)
Why This Order
Allocator → Stdlib → Parser/VM split because:
GlacioJS can now parse JSX (via Yggdrasil) or JS once, cache the bytecode, and inject it into multiple FrostCore runtimes/isolates
The VM becomes smaller — it doesn't need parser tables or lexer state if only running pre-compiled code
It proves the runtime is a true engine that consumes fuel (bytecode), not a monolithic compiler-interpreter
Time Estimate
2–3 weeks
The hard part is decoupling the atom table. quickjs-ng uses a global/runtime-wide atom table for string deduplication and property keys. Making the parser build a local one that gets merged on load requires careful refcount handling.

[444] [assistant_text] The audit result changes Stage 3 fundamentally. Here's what it reveals:

**`JS_WriteObject` / `JS_ReadObject` already exist and already do atom remapping.** They produce a self-contained binary blob with no runtime pointers. The "compilation unit split" from the spec is deferred — that requires rewriting quickjs-ng itself, not wrapping it.

14	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
15	 * Internal runtime struct
16	 *
17	 * registered_subsystems tracks which frost_register_std_*() calls have
18	 * completed so we can enforce dependency ordering and provide idempotency.
19	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
20	struct frost_runtime {
21	    JSRuntime    *js_rt;
22	    JSContext    *js_ctx;
23	    frost_alloc   alloc;               /* copy of caller's vtable */
24	    unsigned int  registered_subsystems; /* bitmask of FROST_STD_* flags */
25	};

27	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
28	 * Default system allocator -- used when caller passes alloc == NULL
29	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
30	static void *sys_calloc(size_t count, size_t size, void *ud)
31	{
32	    (void)ud;
33	    return calloc(count, size);
34	}
35	
36	static void *sys_alloc(size_t size, void *ud)
37	{
38	    (void)ud;
39	    return malloc(size);
40	}
41	
42	static void sys_free(void *ptr, void *ud)
43	{
44	    (void)ud;
45	    free(ptr);
46	}
47	
48	static void *sys_realloc(void *ptr, size_t size, void *ud)
49	{
50	    (void)ud;
51	    return realloc(ptr, size);
52	}
53	
54	static const frost_alloc k_sys_alloc = {
55	    sys_calloc,
56	    sys_alloc,
57	    sys_free,
58	    sys_realloc,
59	    NULL, /* malloc_usable_size -- optional */
60	    NULL  /* userdata */
61	};
62	
63	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
64	 * JSMallocFunctions adapter thunks
65	 *
66	 * quickjs-ng passes opaque as the first arg. We store frost_runtime* there
67	 * so the thunks can reach frost_runtime.alloc.userdata.
68	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
69	static void *thunk_calloc(void *opaque, size_t count, size_t size)
70	{
71	    frost_runtime *fr = (frost_runtime *)opaque;
72	    if (fr->alloc.calloc)
73	        return fr->alloc.calloc(count, size, fr->alloc.userdata);
74	    void *p = fr->alloc.alloc(count * size, fr->alloc.userdata);
75	    if (p) memset(p, 0, count * size);
76	    return p;
77	}
78	
79	static void *thunk_malloc(void *opaque, size_t size)
80	{
81	    frost_runtime *fr = (frost_runtime *)opaque;
82	    return fr->alloc.alloc(size, fr->alloc.userdata);
83	}
84	
85	static void thunk_free(void *opaque, void *ptr)
86	{
87	    frost_runtime *fr = (frost_runtime *)opaque;
88	    fr->alloc.free(ptr, fr->alloc.userdata);
89	}
90	
91	static void *thunk_realloc(void *opaque, void *ptr, size_t size)
92	{
93	    frost_runtime *fr = (frost_runtime *)opaque;
94	    return fr->alloc.realloc(ptr, size, fr->alloc.userdata);
95	}
96	
97	static size_t thunk_usable_size(const void *ptr)
98	{
99	    /* No opaque available -- return 0 so quickjs-ng uses exact sizes. */
100	    (void)ptr;
101	    return 0;
102	}
103	
104	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
105	 * Internal: allocate and wire up a frost_runtime with a JS runtime.
106	 * The JS context is left NULL -- callers set it after.
107	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
108	static frost_runtime *alloc_runtime(const frost_alloc *alloc)
109	{
110	    const frost_alloc *a = alloc ? alloc : &k_sys_alloc;
111	
112	    if (!a->alloc || !a->free || !a->realloc)
113	        return NULL;
114	
115	    frost_runtime *fr = (frost_runtime *)a->alloc(sizeof(frost_runtime), a->userdata);
116	    if (!fr) return NULL;
117	
118	    fr->alloc                = *a;
119	    fr->js_ctx               = NULL;
120	    fr->registered_subsystems = 0;
121	
122	    JSMallocFunctions mf = {
123	        thunk_calloc,
124	        thunk_malloc,
125	        thunk_free,
126	        thunk_realloc,
127	        a->malloc_usable_size ? a->malloc_usable_size : thunk_usable_size,
128	    };
129	
130	    fr->js_rt = JS_NewRuntime2(&mf, (void *)fr);
131	    if (!fr->js_rt) {
132	        a->free(fr, a->userdata);
133	        return NULL;
134	    }
135	
136	    return fr;
137	}
138	
139	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
140	 * Lifecycle -- full stdlib
141	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
142	frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc)
143	{
144	    frost_runtime *fr = alloc_runtime(alloc);
145	    if (!fr) return NULL;
146	
147	    /* JS_NewContext installs the complete quickjs-ng stdlib */
148	    fr->js_ctx = JS_NewContext(fr->js_rt);
149	    if (!fr->js_ctx) {
150	        JS_FreeRuntime(fr->js_rt);
151	        fr->alloc.free(fr, fr->alloc.userdata);
152	        return NULL;
153	    }
154	
155	    /* Mark every subsystem as registered -- it was done by JS_NewContext */
156	    fr->registered_subsystems =
157	        FROST_STD_CORE | FROST_STD_COLLECTIONS |
158	        FROST_STD_ASYNC | FROST_STD_TIME;
159	
160	    return fr;
161	}
162	
163	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
164	 * Lifecycle -- bare runtime (zero stdlib, caller registers subsystems)
165	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
166	frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create_bare(const frost_alloc *alloc)
167	{
168	    frost_runtime *fr = alloc_runtime(alloc);
169	    if (!fr) return NULL;
170	
171	    /* JS_NewContextRaw installs only the bootstrap objects needed for the
172	       VM to function (class prototypes, internal atoms). No JS globals. */
173	    fr->js_ctx = JS_NewContextRaw(fr->js_rt);
174	    if (!fr->js_ctx) {
175	        JS_FreeRuntime(fr->js_rt);
176	        fr->alloc.free(fr, fr->alloc.userdata);
177	        return NULL;
178	    }
179	
180	    /* Enable the C-level eval path (sets ctx->eval_internal).
181	       This does NOT add an `eval` global to JS -- that requires
182	       frost_register_std_core(). Without this, even frost_eval() on
183	       literals like "1+2" would throw "eval is not supported". */
184	    JS_AddIntrinsicEval(fr->js_ctx);
185	
186	    /* registered_subsystems starts at 0 -- nothing installed yet */
187	    return fr;
188	}
189	
190	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
191	 * Lifecycle -- destroy
192	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
193	void frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt)
194	{
195	    if (!rt) return;
196	    void (*free_fn)(void *, void *) = rt->alloc.free;
197	    void *userdata                  = rt->alloc.userdata;
198	
199	    JS_FreeContext(rt->js_ctx);
200	    JS_FreeRuntime(rt->js_rt);
201	    free_fn(rt, userdata);
202	}

204	/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
205	 * Eval
206	 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
207	int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error)
208	{
209	    if (out_error) *out_error = NULL;
210	
211	    size_t len = strlen(source);
212	    JSValue result = JS_Eval(rt->js_ctx, source, len, "<frost>", JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL);
213	
214	    if (!JS_IsException(result)) {
215	        JS_FreeValue(rt->js_ctx, result);
216	        return 0;
217	    }
218	
219	    JS_FreeValue(rt->js_ctx, result);
220	    JSValue exc = JS_GetException(rt->js_ctx);
221	
222	    if (out_error) {
223	        const char *msg = JS_ToCString(rt->js_ctx, exc);
224	        if (msg) {
225	            *out_error = (char *)malloc(strlen(msg) + 1);
226	            if (*out_error) memcpy(*out_error, msg, strlen(msg) + 1);
227	            JS_FreeCString(rt->js_ctx, msg);
228	        }
229	    }
230	
231	    JS_FreeValue(rt->js_ctx, exc);
232	    return -1;
233	}

The library built cleanly -- no warnings on the new files. Here's what Stage 3 delivered:

**`frost/src/frost_parse.c`** — scratch-runtime approach: `JS_NewRuntime` → `JS_Eval(COMPILE_ONLY)` → `JS_WriteObject(BYTECODE|STRIP_SOURCE)` → copy blob to system-`malloc` → destroy scratch runtime. Returns an owning `frost_bytecode*` with no dangling pointers.

**`frost/src/frost_vm.c`** — `frost_runtime_load` deserializes via `JS_ReadObject` and stores the `JSValue` in `rt->loaded_fn`. `frost_runtime_eval_loaded` duplicates the handle with `JS_DupValue` before calling `JS_EvalFunction` so the stored reference survives multiple executions.

**`frost/tests/bytecode_test.c`** — 13 test groups covering: parse success/failure, size, destroy-NULL safety, load/eval basic, parse-once-run-many (5 runtimes), blob independence after scratch runtime gone, bare+std_core target, multi-eval, load replacement, eval-before-load error, and NULL-arg safety.

[586] [assistant_text] Let me read the current README first.
[588] [tool_result]  RESULT: 1	# FrostCore
2	
3	**Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JavaScript engine boundary layer.**
4	
5	FrostCore wraps [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) with a thin C API that gives the embedding layer -- GlacioJS -- explicit control over memory allocation, runtime lifecycle, and JS evaluation. It is not a rewrite of the engine; it is an extraction boundary on top of a living upstream codebase.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## What FrostCore Is
10	
11	| Capability | Status |
12	|---|---|
13	| Per-runtime pluggable allocator | Stage 1 |
14	| Explicit `create` / `destroy` lifecycle (no hidden globals) | Stage 1 |
15	| Multiple runtimes coexisting in one process | Stage 1 |
16	| Minimal `eval` surface for integration testing | Stage 1 |
17	| GC algorithm changes | Not in scope |
18	| Parser/bytecode modularization | Stage 3+ |
19	| Stdlib separation | Stage 3+ |
20	| C++ wrapper | Not in scope |
21	| Task/isolate scheduler | GlacioJS Layer 2 |
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Repository Layout
26	
27	```
28	FrostCore/
29	  quickjs.c / quickjs.h    -- upstream quickjs-ng engine (do not edit)
30	  libregexp.c / libunicode.c / dtoa.c -- upstream support files
31	  CMakeLists.txt / meson.build        -- upstream build (untouched)
32	  README.txt                          -- original quickjs-ng README
33	
34	  frost/                   -- FrostCore overlay (all Stage 1 work lives here)
35	    include/frostcore.h    -- public C API -- the ONLY header GlacioJS imports
36	    src/frostcore.c        -- implementation

46	## Public API (Stage 1)
47	
48	```c
49	#include "frostcore.h"
50	
51	/* Allocator vtable -- all fields except alloc/free/realloc are optional */
52	typedef struct frost_alloc {
53	    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
54	    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
55	    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
56	    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
57	    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr);
58	    void  *userdata;
59	} frost_alloc;
60	
61	/* Pass NULL to use the system allocator */
62	frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
63	void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);
64	
65	/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
66	   *out_error is malloc'd -- caller must free() it. */
67	int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);
68	```

The original flow must be: generate the world inline when Back is pressed from Residents, or Residents is reached differently.

The screen never advanced from World_Setup to Residents automatically — it relied on the user pressing some other button. But there's no such button in `_draw_world_setup`.

[473] [tool_result]  RESULT: 1	# DMLS — Web API & Dashboard Specification
2	
3	> *The island runs. The browser watches.*
4	
5	DMLS exposes a lightweight HTTP REST API and a WebSocket event stream from a parallel thread alongside the Raylib simulation. When Raylib is not initiated (headless mode), the API thread becomes the only interface. A bundled web dashboard connects to both and provides a live browser view of the simulation state.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Architecture
10	
11	```
12	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
13	│                    DMLS Process                     │
14	│                                                     │
15	│  ┌──────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐ │
16	│  │  Simulation Core │    │     API Thread         │ │
17	│  │  (Odin + Epilog) │◄──►│  HTTP REST + WebSocket │ │
18	│  │  [main thread]   │    │  [parallel thread]     │ │
19	│  └──────────────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘ │
20	│                                       │             │
21	└───────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────┘
22	                                        │
23	                          ┌─────────────▼────────────┐
24	                          │    Web Dashboard          │
25	                          │    localhost:7771         │
26	                          │    HTML + JS + WS client  │
27	                          └──────────────────────────┘
28	```
29	
30	### Thread Model
31	
32	- **Main thread** — simulation loop (Raylib if headed, pure tick loop if headless)
33	- **API thread** — HTTP server + WebSocket broadcaster, spawned at startup
34	- **Shared state** — a mutex-protected snapshot struct that the simulation writes every tick and the API thread reads
35	
36	The API thread never touches Epilog directly. It reads only from the snapshot. The simulation thread owns Epilog exclusively.
37	
38	### Headless Mode
39	
40	Launch with `--headless` flag:
41	
42	```sh
43	./dmls --headless
44	./dmls --headless --load save.dmls
45	./dmls --headless --seed 5961641267136C
46	```
47	
48	In headless mode:
49	- Raylib is never initialised
50	- No window is created
51	- Simulation ticks at configured speed (default 1×, configurable via API)
52	- API thread is the only interface
53	- Process runs until `POST /api/control/quit` or SIGINT
54	
55	---
56	
57	## Base URL
58	
59	```
60	http://localhost:7771
61	```
62	
63	Port configurable via `--port` flag or `dmls.cfg`.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Shared Snapshot Struct
68	
69	Written by simulation thread every tick. Read by API thread under mutex.
70	
71	```odin
72	SimSnapshot :: struct {
73	    tick            : u64,
74	    island_name     : string,
75	    seed            : u64,
76	    speed           : u8,          // 0=paused, 1=1x, 4=4x, 16=16x
77	    weather         : string,
78	    time_of_day     : string,      // dawn / day / dusk / night
79	    residents       : [dynamic]ResidentSnapshot,
80	    crushes         : [dynamic]RelationSnapshot,
81	    rivals          : [dynamic]RivalSnapshot,
82	    events          : [dynamic]EventEntry,
83	    is_headless     : bool,
84	}
85	
86	ResidentSnapshot :: struct {
87	    id              : u32,
88	    name            : string,
89	    mood            : string,
90	    position        : [2]i32,
91	    personality     : string,
92	    relationships   : [dynamic]RelationSnapshot,
93	    interaction_counts : map[string]u32,
94	}
95	
96	RelationSnapshot :: struct {
97	    from            : string,
98	    to              : string,
99	    kind            : string,      // crush, friend, acquaintance, sibling, partner, rival
100	}
101	
102	RivalSnapshot :: struct {
103	    a               : string,
104	    b               : string,
105	    duration_ticks  : u32,
106	}
107	
108	EventEntry :: struct {
109	    tick            : u64,
110	    description     : string,
111	    characters      : [dynamic]string,
112	    kind            : string,      // crush_formed, rival_detected, confession, confrontation, decay
113	}
114	```

418	### Server → Client Messages
419	
420	All messages are JSON with a `type` field.
421	
422	---
423	
424	#### tick
425	
426	Sent every simulation tick.
427	
428	```json
429	{
430	  "type": "tick",
431	  "tick": 135,
432	  "speed": 1,
433	  "weather": "clear",
434	  "time_of_day": "day"
435	}
436	```
437	
438	---
439	
440	#### snapshot
441	
442	Full state snapshot. Sent on client connect, and every 10 ticks.
443	
444	```json
445	{
446	  "type": "snapshot",
447	  "tick": 135,
448	  "island_name": "Yggdrasilz",
449	  "seed": "5961641267136C",
450	  "residents": [ /* ResidentSnapshot array */ ],
451	  "crushes": 1,
452	  "rivals": 0,
453	  "events": [ /* last 20 EventEntry */ ]
454	}
455	```
456	
457	---
458	
459	#### event
460	
461	Fired when a social event occurs.
462	
463	```json
464	{
465	  "type": "event",
466	  "tick": 135,
467	  "kind": "crush_formed",
468	  "description": "Anna Croft developed a crush on [NAME]",
469	  "characters": ["Anna Croft", "[NAME]"]
470	}
471	```
472	
473	Event kinds:
474	- `crush_formed`
475	- `crush_resolved` (accepted/rejected)
476	- `rival_detected`
477	- `rival_confrontation`
478	- `friendship_formed`
479	- `friendship_decayed`
480	- `partner_formed`
481	- `mood_changed`
482	- `resident_arrived`
483	- `resident_departed`
484	
485	---
486	
487	#### mood_update
488	
489	Fired when any character's mood changes.
490	
491	```json
492	{
493	  "type": "mood_update",
494	  "character": "Uriel",
495	  "mood": "jealous",
496	  "previous_mood": "lovestruck",
497	  "tick": 136
498	}
499	```
500	
501	---
502	
503	#### position_update
504	
505	Fired every tick for each moving character. Clients use this to animate sprites on the dashboard map.
506	
507	```json
508	{
509	  "type": "position_update",
510	  "updates": [
511	    { "name": "[NAME]",  "position": [129, 140] },
512	    { "name": "Uriel",      "position": [111, 154] },
513	    { "name": "Anna Croft", "position": [122, 147] },
514	    { "name": "Saloni",     "position": [130, 141] }
515	  ],
516	  "tick": 135
517	}
518	```
519	
520	---
521	
522	#### prompt
523	
524	Fired when the simulation is waiting for player input (confession, confrontation). If headless, a prompt sent via WS is the only way to resolve it.
525	
526	```json
527	{
528	  "type": "prompt",
529	  "prompt_id": "conf_uriel_deb_136",
530	  "kind": "confession",
531	  "from": "Uriel",
532	  "to": "[NAME]",
533	  "tick": 136,
534	  "auto_resolve_in_ticks": 10,
535	  "options": ["accept", "reject"]
536	}
537	```
538	
539	Simulation pauses tick progression until prompt is resolved or auto-resolved.
540

544	
545	Sent when a client command fails.

642	│                          │  RESIDENTS                            │
643	│                          │  ● [NAME]    content               │

646	│                          │  ● Saloni       content               │
647	│    Characters as dots    ├───────────────────────────────────────┤
648	│    with mood icons       │  RELATIONSHIPS                        │
649	│    Arrows on hover       │  Uriel → [NAME]     [crush]        │
650	│                          │  [NAME] ↔ Saloni    [sibling]      │

652	│                          ├───────────────────────────────────────┤
653	│                          │  EVENTS                               │
654	│                          │  [135] Uriel approached [NAME]     │
655	│                          │  [128] Anna & Deb traded stories      │
656	│                          │  [089] Rivals detected: Uriel ↔ Anna  │
657	├──────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────┤
658	│  QUERY CONSOLE                                                   │
659	│  ?- rivals(X, Y).    [Run]                                       │
660	│  > X = uriel, Y = anna_croft                                     │
661	└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
662	```
663	
664	---
665	
666	### Dashboard Features
667	
668	- **Live island map** — HTML5 Canvas renders the 256×256 grid. Characters are coloured dots with mood icons. Hover a dot to see relationship arrows drawn to all connected characters.
669	- **Resident list** — live mood and name, coloured per character. Click to expand relationship detail.
670	- **Relationship panel** — all current relationships with kind labels. Rival pairs highlighted in red.
671	- **Event log** — scrollable, last 50 events. Character names colour-coded. New events flash briefly.
672	- **Query console** — type any Epilog query, send via WebSocket, see results inline.
673	- **Speed control** — dropdown: Paused / 1× / 4× / 16×. Updates via WebSocket command.
674	- **Prompt overlay** — when a confession or confrontation fires, a modal appears over the dashboard with Accept/Reject buttons. Sends `resolve_prompt` via WebSocket.
675	- **Connection indicator** — green dot (connected) / red dot (disconnected, auto-reconnect every 3 seconds).
676	
677	---
678	
679	### Dashboard Delivery
680	
681	The dashboard HTML is embedded as a string literal in the Odin API server and served at `GET /`. No external files required. The simulation binary is fully self-contained.
682	
683	```odin
684	DASHBOARD_HTML :: #load("dashboard.html", string)
685	
686	handle_root :: proc(conn: ^HttpConn) {
687	    http_respond(conn, 200, "text/html", DASHBOARD_HTML)
688	}
689	```
690	
691	`dashboard.html` is compiled into the binary at build time via Odin's `#load` directive.
692	
693	---
694	
695	## Implementation Notes
696	
697	### HTTP Server
698	
699	Use a minimal Odin HTTP server — either a thin wrapper over POSIX sockets or a small library. The server needs to handle:
700	- GET and POST only
701	- JSON request/response bodies
702	- WebSocket upgrade handshake (RFC 6455)
703	- One persistent listener thread with a connection pool
704	
705	Do not use a full web framework. The API surface is small enough that raw socket handling is tractable.
706	
707	### Mutex Strategy
708	
709	```odin
710	SimState :: struct {
711	    mu       : sync.Mutex,
712	    snapshot : SimSnapshot,
713	}
714	```
715	
716	Simulation thread:
717	1. Runs tick logic
718	2. Locks mutex
719	3. Writes updated snapshot
720	4. Unlocks mutex
721	
722	API thread:
723	1. Locks mutex
724	2. Reads snapshot (copy to local)
725	3. Unlocks mutex
726	4. Serves response from local copy
727	
728	Mutex hold time is always short — just a struct copy. No Epilog calls inside the lock.
729	
730	### WebSocket Broadcast
731	
732	Maintain a slice of active WebSocket connections. After each tick, the simulation thread signals the API thread via a channel. The API thread reads the snapshot and broadcasts `tick`, `position_update`, and any pending `event` messages to all connected clients.
733	
734	```odin
735	ws_broadcast :: proc(server: ^WsServer, msg: string) {
736	    sync.lock(&server.conn_mu)
737	    defer sync.unlock(&server.conn_mu)
738	    for conn in server.connections {
739	        ws_send(conn, msg)
740	    }
741	}
742	```
743	
744	### Headless Tick Loop
745	
746	```odin
747	headless_loop :: proc(sim: ^Simulation, api: ^ApiServer) {
748	    for !sim.quit {
749	        simulation_tick(sim)
750	        snapshot := build_snapshot(sim)
751	        api_push_snapshot(api, snapshot)
752	        time.sleep(tick_duration(sim.speed))
753	    }
754	}
755	```
756

[483] [tool_result]  RESULT: 1	/*
2	 * sim.odin — Relational simulation tick system (M5).
3	 *
4	 * Every simulation tick:
5	 *   1. Characters near each other accumulate interaction_count in Epilog.
6	 *   2. Dependent RNG decides if a crush develops.
7	 *   3. Eligible check (Epilog query) gates crush formation.
8	 *   4. Mood is re-derived each tick from relationship state.
9	 *   5. Events are appended to the rolling event log.
10	 *
11	 * The Epilog engine is always the source of truth for social state.
12	 * Odin never caches relationship facts — it queries every tick.
13	 */
14	
15	package dmls
16	
17	import "core:fmt"
18	import "core:strings"
19	
20	// ---- Event log -------------------------------------------------------------
21	
22	MAX_EVENTS   :: 20
23	EVENT_MSG_LEN :: 96
24	
25	EventEntry :: struct {
26	    tick : u64,
27	    msg  : [EVENT_MSG_LEN]u8,
28	}
29	
30	EventLog :: struct {
31	    entries : [MAX_EVENTS]EventEntry,
32	    head    : int,   // ring-buffer write index
33	    count   : int,
34	}
35	
36	event_log_push :: proc(log: ^EventLog, tick: u64, msg: string) {
37	    e := &log.entries[log.head]
38	    e.tick = tick
39	    n := min(len(msg), EVENT_MSG_LEN - 1)
40	    copy(e.msg[:], msg[:n])
41	    e.msg[n] = 0
42	    log.head  = (log.head + 1) % MAX_EVENTS
43	    if log.count < MAX_EVENTS { log.count += 1 }
44	}
45	
46	// Iterate from newest to oldest (newest first).
47	event_log_get :: proc(log: ^EventLog, i: int) -> ^EventEntry {
48	    if i >= log.count do return nil
49	    idx := (log.head - 1 - i + MAX_EVENTS * 2) % MAX_EVENTS
50	    return &log.entries[idx]
51	}
52	
53	event_entry_str :: proc(e: ^EventEntry) -> string {
54	    return strings.truncate_to_byte(string(e.msg[:]), 0)
55	}
56	
57	// ---- Mood ------------------------------------------------------------------
58	
59	Mood :: enum u8 {
60	    Content,
61	    Happy,
62	    Sad,
63	    Lovestruck,
64	    Jealous,
65	}
66	
67	mood_label :: proc(m: Mood) -> string {
68	    switch m {
69	    case .Content:    return "content"
70	    case .Happy:      return "happy"
71	    case .Sad:        return "sad"
72	    case .Lovestruck: return "lovestruck"
73	    case .Jealous:    return "jealous"
74	    }
75	    return "content"
76	}

78	// Per-character social state (derived each tick — NOT authoritative, just cache).
79	CharSocial :: struct {
80	    mood             : Mood,
81	    interaction_count: u32,   // total lifetime interactions (also in Epilog)
82	    has_crush        : bool,
83	}
84	
85	// ---- Simulation state ------------------------------------------------------
86	
87	SimState :: struct {
88	    rng      : DependentRNG,
89	    social   : [MAX_RESIDENTS]CharSocial,
90	    log      : EventLog,
91	    // Counters displayed in stats panel
92	    crush_count : int,
93	    rival_count : int,
94	}
95	
96	sim_init :: proc(s: ^SimState, seed: u64) {
97	    s^ = {}
98	    dependent_rng_init(&s.rng, seed, 0xC0FFEE_CAFE_1234)
99	}
