## Anti-Patterns

**Never do these when implementing MD3:**

- **Mix MD2 and MD3 libraries**: Don't use `@material/mdc-*` (MD2) alongside `@material/web` (MD3). They have incompatible APIs and styling.
- **Hardcode colors**: Always use `var(--md-sys-color-*)` tokens, never raw hex/rgb values. Hardcoded colors break dynamic theming, dark mode, and contrast adjustment.
- **Ignore tonal pairing**: Only combine colors in their intended pairs (e.g., `primary` + `on-primary`, `surface-container` + `on-surface`). Arbitrary pairings break contrast in dynamic color and high contrast modes.
- **Use `outline` for dividers**: Use `outline-variant` for dividers. `outline` is for important boundaries like text field borders.
- **Import all of @material/web**: Always import individual component modules. Barrel imports include every component and destroy bundle size.
- **Use `border-radius` directly**: Use shape tokens (`var(--md-sys-shape-corner-medium)`) so shapes stay consistent with theming.
- **Use shadows for elevation by default**: MD3 communicates elevation through tonal surface color, not shadows. Only add shadows when elements need extra separation from busy backgrounds.
- **Apply frontend-design "avoid Roboto" rule**: On **Android**, **Roboto** is the default Material typeface; **web** often uses Roboto or Roboto Flex with MD3 tokens. Replace only when intentionally customizing the type scale.
- **Assume SSR compatibility**: `@material/web` uses Web Components (custom elements) which require JavaScript to render. They won't produce meaningful HTML in SSR without additional hydration strategies.
- **Ignore foldables and large screens**: MD3 is designed for all screen sizes. Don't ship phone-only layouts — use canonical layouts, multi-pane at 600dp+, and test on foldable/tablet emulators. Place no interactive content across the fold/hinge.
- **Stretch content to fill wide screens**: On Large (1200dp+) and Extra-large (1600dp+) windows, constrain content to a max width (840–1040dp). Endless-width text lines are unreadable.

## Platform Notes

### Flutter
```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.deepPurple),
  ),
);
```

### Jetpack Compose
See **[Jetpack Compose (primary)](#jetpack-compose-primary)** above. Use `LocalContext.current` with `dynamicLightColorScheme` / `dynamicDarkColorScheme` only when `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S` and dynamic color is enabled; otherwise supply static light/dark schemes.

### Component Name Mapping
| Concept | Web | Flutter | Compose |
|---------|-----|---------|---------|
| Filled button | `md-filled-button` | `FilledButton` | `Button` |
| Outlined text field | `md-outlined-text-field` | `OutlinedTextField` | `OutlinedTextField` |
| FAB | `md-fab` | `FloatingActionButton` | `FloatingActionButton` |
| Navigation bar | `md-navigation-bar` | `NavigationBar` | `NavigationBar` |
| Switch | `md-switch` | `Switch` | `Switch` |

## M3 Expressive (May 2025)

The Expressive update adds visual richness while maintaining usability. **Availability differs by platform** — do not assume one stack implements everything.

| Capability | Jetpack Compose | Flutter | Web (`@material/web`) |
|------------|-----------------|---------|------------------------|
| Expressive layout scaffold / adaptive layout | Compose-first via Material3 adaptive APIs and window size classes | Use Flutter adaptive/layout primitives | CSS/container queries/manual layout; no Material Web parity |
| 8dp spacing system | Use design tokens / `Dp` spacing constants; keep margins, padding, and gaps adaptive | Use theme spacing constants | CSS custom properties / design tokens |
| Expressive lists, menus, search, search app bar | Primary target per current Material guidance; check BOM and opt-ins | Check current Flutter Material docs | Spec-aligned custom implementation; `@material/web` is maintenance-only |
| Spring / motion physics | Supported in Material 3 (see `MotionScheme`, expressive APIs per BOM) | Varies by Flutter Material version | **Not** in Material Web; use easing/duration or custom motion |
| Emphasized typography | Via theme / type scale | Via theme | Token/CSS only; no full Expressive component set |
| Shape morphing | Compose-first in Google’s expressive rollout | Check current Flutter docs | **Not** in `@material/web` |
| New button sizes (XS–XL), toggle | Follow Compose Material3 components | Follow Flutter MD3 | Height/CSS approximations only |
| Extra corner tokens (e.g. large-increased) | `MaterialTheme.shapes` / tokens | Theme shapes | CSS `--md-sys-shape-*` |
| 3 contrast levels | Scheme builders / system | Plugins / manual | `SchemeContent` contrast parameter in JS utilities |
| Watches / XR form factors | Use Compose/Wear/XR-specific guidance where available | Platform-specific | Web/spatial UI custom implementation |

**Web:** [Material Web is maintenance-only; M3 Expressive is not on Web](https://m3.material.io/develop/web). Use CSS easing/duration tokens as fallback for motion, not spring parity.

**Legacy easing/duration** remains valid for **transitions** (enter/exit/shared-axis) where the spec still references them; see the Motion table below.

## MD3 Compliance Audit

When invoked with `audit` as the argument (e.g., `/material-3 audit`), or when asked to audit/review MD3 compliance, analyze the target app or page and produce a compliance report.

### Audit Procedure

1. **Identify the target**: The user provides a URL (use browser tools to inspect), file paths (read source), or a running app.
2. **Inspect the following categories** and score each 0–10:

| Category | What to check |
|----------|--------------|
| **Color tokens** | **Web:** `--md-sys-color-*` / generated CSS. **Compose:** `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` roles (no arbitrary `Color(...)` for surfaces without reason). Proper tonal pairing (`onX` on `X`). Dark theme. **Flutter:** `ColorScheme` roles. |
| **Typography** | MD3 type scale: **Compose** `MaterialTheme.typography`; **web** typescale tokens; correct roles (Display, Headline, Title, Body, Label). |
| **Shape** | **Compose** `MaterialTheme.shapes` / component `Shape`; **web** `var(--md-sys-shape-*)`. Buttons: full; cards: medium; avoid magic numbers. |
| **Elevation** | Tonal elevation (`Surface` tonal/shadow as appropriate). **Web:** hover/focus where relevant. |
| **Components** | **Compose:** Material3 composables (`Button`, `Scaffold`, etc.). **Web:** `@material/web` or spec-aligned HTML/CSS. Correct variants. |
| **Layout** | Canonical layouts; **Compose** window size class / adaptive APIs; readable max width on large widths; foldable hinge avoidance. |
| **Navigation** | Bar / rail / drawer / drawers+**Compose** `NavHost` patterns per size class; predictive back where applicable. |
| **Motion** | **Compose** `MotionScheme` / expressive APIs when used; transitions may still use easing/duration. **Web:** CSS motion tokens fallback. |
| **Accessibility** | MD3 roles help, but **verify contrast**: UI components often need **3:1** for large text/borders and **4.5:1** for normal text (WCAG 2.x). TalkBack/semantics (Compose), focus order, touch targets (~48dp). **Web:** ARIA, keyboard. |
| **Theming** | **Compose:** `MaterialTheme` + light/dark/dynamic as designed. **Web:** CSS custom properties on `:root` or subtree. **Flutter:** `ThemeData` + `ColorScheme`. |

3. **Generate the report**:

```
# MD3 Compliance Audit Report

Target: [URL or file path]
Date: [date]
Overall Score: [X/100]

## Scores by Category
| Category       | Score | Status |
|----------------|-------|--------|
| Color tokens   | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Typography     | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Shape          | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Elevation      | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Components     | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Layout         | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Navigation     | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Motion         | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Accessibility  | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |
| Theming        | X/10  | [pass/warn/fail] |

## Critical Issues
[List items scoring 0-3 with specific file:line references and fixes]

## Warnings
[List items scoring 4-6 with recommendations]

## Passing
[List items scoring 7-10 with notes on what's done well]

## Recommended Fixes (Priority Order)
1. [Most impactful fix first]
2. ...
```

### Audit Methods

**For a live URL** (browser or devtools):
- Inspect computed styles and CSS variables (`--md-sys-*`)
- Resize viewport or use responsive mode for breakpoints
- Capture screenshots at key widths if helpful

**For source code** (file paths provided):
- **Compose/Kotlin:** `.kt` files — `MaterialTheme`, composables, `Color(0x…)` abuse, hard-coded `Dp`, missing `Modifier.semantics` where needed
- **Flutter:** `.dart` — `ThemeData`, `ColorScheme`
- **Web:** HTML/JSX/Vue/Svelte; CSS/SCSS for tokens
- Check **web** imports for `@material/web` vs `@material/mdc-*` (MD2)

**Quick checks** (adapt paths to your stack):
```
# Web: hardcoded colors
grep -rn '#[0-9a-fA-F]\{3,8\}' --include='*.css' --include='*.scss'

# Compose: raw Color(...) audits (sample — tune for your codebase)
grep -rn 'Color(0x' --include='*.kt'

# MD2 on web
grep -rn '@material/mdc-' --include='*.js' --include='*.ts'
```

**Browser automation** (if your environment exposes MCP browser tools): navigate, snapshot DOM/CSS variables, resize for breakpoints — optional, not required.

### Scoring Guide

- **9-10**: Fully MD3 compliant, uses correct tokens and patterns
- **7-8**: Mostly compliant, minor issues (e.g., a few hardcoded values)
- **4-6**: Partially compliant, some MD3 patterns but significant gaps
- **1-3**: Major violations, mostly non-MD3 or MD2 patterns
- **0**: Not applicable or completely absent

Status thresholds: **pass** (7+), **warn** (4-6), **fail** (0-3)

But `headers_str` is `s[:split]` where `s = string(raw)` — `raw` is a `[8192]u8` local in `_conn_thread`. That's still alive when `ctx.handler(req, ctx.sock)` is called since `_conn_thread` hasn't returned yet. So the slice is valid.

Let me check the actual parse more carefully — specifically whether `split_lines` returns substrings of the original or new allocations:

`strings.split_lines` in Odin typically returns slices into the original string (no allocation for the substrings themselves). So `lines[0]` is a substring of `headers_str`. `strings.fields` similarly returns subslices. Then `full_path = parts[1]` is a subslice. `strings.clone(full_path, ...)` copies it. So `req.path` is properly allocated on `temp_allocator`.

The real problem: `strings.split_lines` takes a `string` but we're passing the `context.temp_allocator` — wait, the signature is `strings.split_lines(s: string, allocator := context.allocator) -> []string`. It allocates the `[]string` slice on the allocator, but the string contents are subslices. So `lines` itself is allocated. And `strings.fields(lines[0], context.temp_allocator)` similarly allocates `parts`. These are all fine.

167	route_events :: proc(query: string) -> string {
168	    snap  := shared_read_snapshot()
169	    b     := strings.builder_make(context.temp_allocator)

171	    kind_filter := ""
172	
173	    // Parse ?limit=N&kind=K
174	    for part in strings.split(query, "&", context.temp_allocator) {
175	        kv := strings.split(part, "=", context.temp_allocator)
176	        if len(kv) != 2 do continue
177	        switch kv[0] {
178	        case "limit":
179	            if n, ok := strconv.parse_int(kv[1]); ok { limit = n }
180	        case "kind":
181	            kind_filter = kv[1]
182	        }
183	    }
184	
185	    strings.write_string(&b, `{"events":[`)
186	    count := 0
187	    first := true
188	    for i in 0..<snap.event_count {
189	        if count >= limit do break
190	        e := &snap.events[i]
191	        kind := _snap_cstr(e.kind[:])
192	        if kind_filter != "" && kind != kind_filter do continue
193	        desc := _snap_cstr(e.description[:])
194	        if !first { strings.write_string(&b, ",") }
195	        first = false
196	        fmt.sbprintf(&b, `{"tick":%d,"kind":"%s","description":"%s","characters":[]}`,
197	            e.tick, kind, _json_escape(desc, context.temp_allocator))
198	        count += 1
199	    }
200	    strings.write_string(&b, "]}")
201	    return strings.to_string(b)
202	}
203	
204	_json_escape :: proc(s: string, alloc := context.allocator) -> string {
205	    b := strings.builder_make(alloc)
206	    for c in s {
207	        switch c {
208	        case '"':  strings.write_string(&b, `\"`)
209	        case '\\': strings.write_string(&b, `\\`)
210	        case '\n': strings.write_string(&b, `\n`)
211	        case '\r': strings.write_string(&b, `\r`)
212	        case:      strings.write_rune(&b, c)
213	        }
214	    }
215	    return strings.to_string(b)
216	}

290	// ---- /api/query (Epilog read-only proxy) ----------------------------------
291	// The query must be forwarded to the sim thread, which owns the engine.
292	// We use a simple request/response slot in g_shared.
293	
294	EpilogQueryReq :: struct {
295	    goal   : [256]u8,
296	    goal_len : int,
297	    pending  : bool,
298	    done     : bool,
299	    result   : [4096]u8,
300	    result_len : int,
301	}
302	
303	// We expose a single-slot query channel; concurrent queries are serialised.
304	g_eq_mu  : ^_EqState
305	_EqState :: struct {
306	    mu      : _sync_mu,
307	    req     : EpilogQueryReq,
308	}
309	
310	// minimal mutex alias to avoid import cycle
311	_sync_mu :: struct { _: [8]u8 } // placeholder — we reuse sync.Mutex via g_shared
312	
313	// Because we can't block the API thread indefinitely, we use a polling approach:
314	// API thread writes goal into g_shared, sim thread picks it up each tick.
315	
316	shared_eq_req   : EpilogQueryReq
317	shared_eq_mu    : _DummyMu  // we re-use the snapshot mutex
318	
319	_DummyMu :: struct{}
320	
321	// Actually we'll piggyback on the snapshot mutex for the query channel.
322	
323	shared_set_query :: proc(goal: string) {
324	    sync.lock(&g_shared.mu)
325	    n := min(len(goal), 255)
326	    copy(shared_eq_req.goal[:], goal[:n])
327	    shared_eq_req.goal[n]  = 0
328	    shared_eq_req.goal_len = n
329	    shared_eq_req.pending  = true
330	    shared_eq_req.done     = false
331	    sync.unlock(&g_shared.mu)
332	}
333	
334	shared_poll_query :: proc() -> (goal: string, pending: bool) {
335	    sync.lock(&g_shared.mu)
336	    defer sync.unlock(&g_shared.mu)
337	    if !shared_eq_req.pending do return "", false
338	    shared_eq_req.pending = false
339	    g := strings.truncate_to_byte(string(shared_eq_req.goal[:]), 0)
340	    return strings.clone(g, context.temp_allocator), true
341	}
342	
343	shared_put_query_result :: proc(result: string) {
344	    sync.lock(&g_shared.mu)
345	    n := min(len(result), 4095)
346	    copy(shared_eq_req.result[:], result[:n])
347	    shared_eq_req.result[n]    = 0
348	    shared_eq_req.result_len   = n
349	    shared_eq_req.done         = true
350	    sync.unlock(&g_shared.mu)
351	}
352	
353	shared_get_query_result :: proc() -> (result: string, done: bool) {
354	    sync.lock(&g_shared.mu)
355	    defer sync.unlock(&g_shared.mu)
356	    if !shared_eq_req.done do return "", false
357	    shared_eq_req.done = false
358	    r := strings.truncate_to_byte(string(shared_eq_req.result[:]), 0)
359	    return strings.clone(r, context.temp_allocator), true
360	}

362	// Forbidden patterns for read-only query gate
363	_query_forbidden :: proc(goal: string) -> bool {
364	    gl := strings.to_lower(goal, context.temp_allocator)
365	    return strings.contains(gl, "assert") || strings.contains(gl, "retract")
366	}
367	
368	route_query :: proc(body: string) -> (string, int) {
369	    goal, ok := _json_get_str(body, "goal")
370	    if !ok {
371	        return `{"error":"missing goal field"}`, 400
372	    }
373	    if _query_forbidden(goal) {
374	        return `{"error":"assert and retract are not permitted via the query API"}`, 403
375	    }
376	    return fmt.tprintf(`{"goal":"%s","results":[],"count":0,"note":"query forwarding not yet wired in this build"}`,
377	        _json_escape(goal, context.temp_allocator)), 200
378	}

381	
382	route_add_resident_json :: proc(body: string) -> (string, int) {
383	    // Parse name — minimal JSON key extraction
384	    name, ok := _json_get_str(body, "name")
385	    if !ok || len(name) == 0 {
386	        return `{"error":"name required"}`, 400
387	    }
388	    // Signal sim thread to add a resident.  For now we write to a small shared
389	    // channel; the sim thread processes it next tick.
390	    shared_request_add_resident(name, body)
391	    return fmt.tprintf(`{"spawned":true,"name":"%s"}`, _json_escape(name, context.temp_allocator)), 202
392	}

395	    if len(name) == 0 {
396	        return `{"error":"name required"}`, 400
397	    }

399	    b := strings.builder_make(context.temp_allocator)
400	    snap := shared_read_snapshot()
401	    fmt.sbprintf(&b, `{"removed":"%s","at_tick":%d}`, name, snap.tick)
402	    return strings.to_string(b), 200
403	}

405	// Resident add/remove request channel
406	ResidentReq :: struct {
407	    kind : u8,    // 0=add 1=remove
408	    name : [MAX_SNAP_NAME]u8,
409	    body : [512]u8,
410	}
411	
412	g_res_req : ResidentReq
413	g_res_req_pending : bool
414	g_res_req_mu      : bool  // spin via shared mu
415	
416	shared_request_add_resident :: proc(name, body: string) {
417	    sync.lock(&g_shared.mu)
418	    g_res_req.kind = 0
419	    _snap_str(g_res_req.name[:], name)
420	    n := min(len(body), 511)
421	    copy(g_res_req.body[:], body[:n])
422	    g_res_req.body[n] = 0
423	    g_res_req_pending = true
424	    sync.unlock(&g_shared.mu)
425	}
426	
427	shared_request_remove_resident :: proc(name: string) {
428	    sync.lock(&g_shared.mu)
429	    g_res_req.kind = 1
430	    _snap_str(g_res_req.name[:], name)
431	    g_res_req_pending = true
432	    sync.unlock(&g_shared.mu)
433	}
434	
435	shared_poll_res_req :: proc() -> (kind: u8, name: string, body: string, pending: bool) {
436	    sync.lock(&g_shared.mu)
437	    defer sync.unlock(&g_shared.mu)
438	    if !g_res_req_pending do return 0, "", "", false
439	    g_res_req_pending = false
440	    name = strings.clone(strings.truncate_to_byte(string(g_res_req.name[:]), 0), context.temp_allocator)
441	    body = strings.clone(strings.truncate_to_byte(string(g_res_req.body[:]), 0), context.temp_allocator)
442	    return g_res_req.kind, name, body, true
443	}

445	// ---- WebSocket message handler (called per connected client frame) ----------
446	
447	ws_handle_message :: proc(msg: string, sock: net.TCP_Socket) {
448	    // Expect JSON with "type" field
449	    typ, ok := _json_get_str(msg, "type")
450	    if !ok do return
451	
452	    switch typ {
453	    case "set_speed":
454	        speed_val, sok := _json_get_int(msg, "speed")
455	        if !sok {
456	            ws_send_sock(sock, `{"type":"error","message":"missing speed"}`)
457	            return
458	        }
459	        idx, valid := _speed_index_from_val(speed_val)
460	        if !valid {
461	            b := strings.builder_make(context.temp_allocator)
462	            fmt.sbprintf(&b, `{"type":"error","message":"unknown speed value: %d","original_command":%s}`,
463	                speed_val, msg)
464	            ws_send_sock(sock, strings.to_string(b))
465	            return
466	        }
467	        shared_set_speed_req(idx)
468	
469	    case "pause":
470	        shared_set_speed_req(0)
471	
472	    case "unpause":
473	        shared_set_speed_req(1)
474	
475	    case "resolve_prompt":
476	        pid, _ := _json_get_str(msg, "prompt_id")
477	        choice_str, _ := _json_get_str(msg, "choice")
478	        choice := 0
479	        if choice_str == "accept" { choice = 1 }
480	        else if choice_str == "reject" { choice = 2 }
481	        if !shared_resolve_prompt(pid, choice) {
482	            ws_send_sock(sock, `{"type":"error","message":"no matching prompt"}`)
483	        }
484	
485	    case "query":
486	        goal, gok := _json_get_str(msg, "goal")
487	        if !gok {
488	            ws_send_sock(sock, `{"type":"error","message":"missing goal"}`)
489	            return
490	        }
491	        if _query_forbidden(goal) {
492	            ws_send_sock(sock, `{"type":"error","message":"assert/retract forbidden"}`)
493	            return
494	        }
495	        // Return empty result immediately (same limitation as REST /api/query)
496	        b := strings.builder_make(context.temp_allocator)
497	        fmt.sbprintf(&b, `{"type":"query_result","goal":"%s","results":[],"count":0}`,
498	            _json_escape(goal, context.temp_allocator))
499	        ws_send_sock(sock, strings.to_string(b))
500	
501	    case "add_resident":
502	        name, _ := _json_get_str(msg, "name")
503	        if len(name) > 0 {
504	            shared_request_add_resident(name, msg)
505	        }
506	    }
507	}
508	
509	// Send a text frame to a single WS connection
510	ws_send_sock :: proc(sock: net.TCP_Socket, msg: string) {
511	    frame := ws_make_frame(msg)
512	    defer delete(frame)
513	    net.send_tcp(sock, frame)
514	}

516	// ---- Minimal JSON value extractors -----------------------------------------
517	
518	_json_get_str :: proc(json: string, key: string) -> (string, bool) {
519	    pat := strings.concatenate({`"`, key, `"`}, context.temp_allocator)
520	    i := strings.index(json, pat)
521	    if i < 0 do return "", false
522	    rest := json[i + len(pat):]
523	    ci := strings.index(rest, ":")
524	    if ci < 0 do return "", false
525	    rest = strings.trim_space(rest[ci+1:])
526	    if len(rest) == 0 || rest[0] != '"' do return "", false
527	    rest = rest[1:]
528	    end := strings.index(rest, `"`)
529	    if end < 0 do return "", false
530	    return rest[:end], true
531	}
532	
533	_json_get_int :: proc(json: string, key: string) -> (int, bool) {
534	    pat := strings.concatenate({`"`, key, `"`}, context.temp_allocator)
535	    i := strings.index(json, pat)
536	    if i < 0 do return 0, false
537	    rest := json[i + len(pat):]
538	    ci := strings.index(rest, ":")
539	    if ci < 0 do return 0, false
540	    rest = strings.trim_space(rest[ci+1:])
541	    // Read digits
542	    end := 0
543	    for end < len(rest) && (rest[end] >= '0' && rest[end] <= '9') { end += 1 }
544	    if end == 0 do return 0, false
545	    v, ok := strconv.parse_int(rest[:end])
546	    return v, ok
547	}

549	// ---- Main HTTP dispatcher --------------------------------------------------
550	
551	DASHBOARD_HTML :: #load("dashboard.html", string)
552	
553	api_dispatch :: proc(req: HttpRequest, sock: net.TCP_Socket) {
554	    free_all(context.temp_allocator)
555	    defer free_all(context.temp_allocator)
556	
557	    // WebSocket upgrade
558	    if req.is_ws_upgrade && req.path == "/ws" {
559	        if !ws_handshake(sock, req.ws_key) do return
560	        ws_hub_add(sock)
561	
562	        // Send initial snapshot
563	        snap_json := _build_snapshot_json()
564	        ws_send_sock(sock, snap_json)
565	
566	        // Read loop
567	        for {
568	            msg, closed := ws_read_frame(sock)
569	            if closed { break }
570	            if len(msg) > 0 {
571	                ws_handle_message(msg, sock)
572	            }
573	        }
574	        ws_hub_remove(sock)
575	        return
576	    }
577	
578	    // REST routes
579	    resp := HttpResponse{}
580	    switch req.method {
581	    case .GET:
582	        switch {
583	        case req.path == "/":
584	            resp = http_ok(DASHBOARD_HTML, "text/html")
585	
586	        case req.path == "/api/status":
587	            resp = http_ok(route_status())
588	
589	        case req.path == "/api/residents":
590	            resp = http_ok(route_residents())
591	
592	        case strings.has_prefix(req.path, "/api/residents/"):
593	            name := req.path[len("/api/residents/"):]
594	            body, code := route_resident_by_name(name)
595	            resp = HttpResponse{status = code, content = body, ctype = "application/json"}
596	
597	        case req.path == "/api/relationships":
598	            resp = http_ok(route_relationships())
599	
600	        case req.path == "/api/rivals":
601	            resp = http_ok(route_rivals())
602	
603	        case req.path == "/api/events":
604	            resp = http_ok(route_events(req.query))
605	
606	        case req.path == "/api/query":
607	            body, code := route_query(req.body)
608	            resp = HttpResponse{status = code, content = body, ctype = "application/json"}
609	
610	        case:
611	            resp = http_err(404, `{"error":"not found"}`)
612	        }
613	
614	    case .POST:
615	        switch req.path {
616	        case "/api/control/speed":
617	            body, code := route_control_speed(req.body)
618	            resp = HttpResponse{status = code, content = body, ctype = "application/json"}
619	        case "/api/control/pause":
620	            resp = http_ok(route_control_pause())
621	        case "/api/control/save":
622	            resp = http_ok(route_control_save())
623	        case "/api/control/quit":
624	            resp = http_ok(route_control_quit())
625	        case "/api/residents":
626	            body, code := route_add_resident_json(req.body)
627	            resp = HttpResponse{status = code, content = body, ctype = "application/json"}
628	        case "/api/query":
629	            body, code := route_query(req.body)
630	            resp = HttpResponse{status = code, content = body, ctype = "application/json"}
631	        case:
632	            resp = http_err(404, `{"error":"not found"}`)
633	        }
634	
635	    case .DELETE:
636	        if strings.has_prefix(req.path, "/api/residents/") {
637	            name := req.path[len("/api/residents/"):]
638	            body, code := route_remove_resident(name)
639	            resp = HttpResponse{status = code, content = body, ctype = "application/json"}
640	        } else {
641	            resp = http_err(404, `{"error":"not found"}`)
642	        }
643	
644	    case .UNKNOWN:
645	        resp = http_err(405, `{"error":"method not allowed"}`)
646	    }
647	
648	    http_send(sock, resp)
649	}

651	// Build a WS "snapshot" message
652	_build_snapshot_json :: proc() -> string {
653	    snap := shared_read_snapshot()
654	    b    := strings.builder_make(context.temp_allocator)
655	
656	    strings.write_string(&b, `{"type":"snapshot",`)
657	    _js_u64(&b, "tick", snap.tick); strings.write_string(&b, ",")
658	    _js_str(&b, "island_name", _snap_cstr(snap.island_name[:])); strings.write_string(&b, ",")
659	    fmt.sbprintf(&b, `"seed":"%016X"`, snap.seed); strings.write_string(&b, ",")
660	    _js_int(&b, "crushes", snap.crush_count); strings.write_string(&b, ",")
661	    _js_int(&b, "rivals", snap.rival_count); strings.write_string(&b, `,"residents":[`)
662	    for i in 0..<snap.resident_count {
663	        if i > 0 { strings.write_string(&b, ",") }
664	        _resident_json(&snap.residents[i], &b)
665	    }
666	    strings.write_string(&b, `],"events":[`)
667	    for i in 0..<min(snap.event_count, 20) {
668	        if i > 0 { strings.write_string(&b, ",") }
669	        e := &snap.events[i]
670	        fmt.sbprintf(&b, `{"tick":%d,"kind":"%s","description":"%s"}`,
671	            e.tick, _snap_cstr(e.kind[:]),
672	            _json_escape(_snap_cstr(e.description[:]), context.temp_allocator))
673	    }
674	    strings.write_string(&b, "]}")
675	    return strings.to_string(b)
676	}

This means any string data that was allocated on the temp allocator during `_parse_request` is now freed, including `req.path`! The `req.path` slice now points to freed memory, which may appear to contain garbage and fail the `==` comparison.

The fix: don't free the temp allocator at the top of `api_dispatch`. The defer at the end is sufficient — free only at the end, not at the start. The initial `free_all` was meant to flush any leftover temp data from prior work, but the path was just parsed and lives on `context.temp_allocator`.

104	_parse_seed :: proc(s: string) -> (u64, bool) {
105	    val := u64(0)
106	    if len(s) == 0 do return 0, false
107	    for ch in s {
108	        switch ch {
109	        case '0'..='9': val = val * 16 + u64(ch - '0')
110	        case 'a'..='f': val = val * 16 + u64(ch - 'a' + 10)
111	        case 'A'..='F': val = val * 16 + u64(ch - 'A' + 10)
112	        case: return 0, false
113	        }
114	    }
115	    return val, true
116	}

I found comprehensive information about NASA and JPL's C coding standards. Here's what I discovered:

## Overview

The Power of 10 Rules were created in 2006 by Gerard J. Holzmann of the NASA/JPL Laboratory for Reliable Software. The rules are intended to eliminate certain C coding practices that make code difficult to review or statically analyze. These rules are a complement to the MISRA C guidelines and have been incorporated into the greater set of JPL coding standards.

## Key Rules

The 10 main rules include:

1. Restrict all code to very simple control flow constructs—do not use goto statements, setjmp or longjmp constructs, or direct or indirect recursion.

2. Give all loops a fixed upper bound—it must be trivially possible for a checking tool to prove statically that the loop cannot exceed a preset upper bound on the number of iterations.

3. Do not use dynamic memory allocation after initialization.

4. No function should be longer than what can be printed on a single sheet of paper in a standard format with one line per statement and one line per declaration.

5. Each calling function must check the return value of nonvoid functions, and each called function must check the validity of all parameters provided by the caller.

6. The use of the preprocessor must be limited to the inclusion of header files and simple macros definitions—token pasting, variable argument lists (ellipses), and recursive macro calls are not allowed.

7. The use of pointers must be restricted—specifically, no more than one level of dereference should be used.

8. All code must be compiled, from the first day of development, with all compiler warnings enabled at the most pedantic setting available.

## Formal Standard

The relatively effortless adoption of the Power of Ten rules led to the creation of a new formal "JPL Institutional Coding Standard" that combines the Power of Ten rules with a small number of additional rules that are more specific to the spacecraft context.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about JPL C coding standards:

## Overview
The JPL Coding Standard for C programming language defines rules across several levels of compliance that primarily target the development of mission critical flight software. The JPL code standards are based on the 2004 MISRA-C coding standard.

## Key Areas Covered

**Static Analysis and Compilation:**
Among the requirements for C-language code at JPL: Compile with all warnings enabled; use static source code analyzers.

**Function Length:**
Use short functions with a limited number of parameters. Additionally, the ability to customize the rules allows for quick experimentation, such as by defining the limit on function length, or the minimal number of assertions per functions of a given minimal size.

**General Rules:**
The rules focus on aspects like language compliance, predictable execution, defensive coding and code clarity, addressing issues like loop bounds, recursion, memory protection, assertions and limiting preprocessor usage.

**Preprocessor Usage:**
In some cases, the JPL Coding Standard puts additional restriction on what features of C can be used—preprocessor features are especially constrained.

**Key design decisions following JPL rules:**

| Rule | How it's applied |
|------|-----------------|
| No recursion | `var_walk` is an explicit `for` loop; `probe_slot` is a linear scan |
| Fixed loop bounds | Every loop caps at `ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY` or `VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY` |
| No post-init malloc | All storage is pre-declared inside `AtomTable` / `VarRegistry` |
| Pointer depth ≤ 1 | `entry_at()` returns a single-level `VarEntry *`; no `**` anywhere |
| Parameter validation | Every public function returns `-1` / `ATOM_ID_INVALID` on bad input |
| Assertions | `assert()` guards internal invariants (full table before insert, etc.) |
| `strncpy` avoided | Used `memcpy` + explicit NUL to dodge the MSVC deprecation warning |

2	 * atoms.c — Atom table implementation for the Epilog inference engine.
3	 *
4	 * Strategy: open-addressed hash table with linear probing.
5	 * All storage is pre-allocated in AtomTable (no malloc after init).
6	 *
7	 * JPL rules observed:
8	 *   Rule 1  — no goto, no setjmp/longjmp, no recursion.
9	 *   Rule 2  — every loop has a fixed upper bound (ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY).
10	 *   Rule 3  — no dynamic memory allocation after atom_table_init().
11	 *   Rule 4  — no function exceeds ~60 lines.
12	 *   Rule 5  — every parameter validated; every return value is meaningful.
13	 *   Rule 6  — preprocessor used only for include and simple constants.
14	 *   Rule 7  — pointer depth ≤ 1 in all operations.
15	 *   Rule 8  — compiled with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic.
16	 */
17	
18	#include "../include/atoms.h"
19	
20	#include <assert.h>   /* assert()   */
21	#include <string.h>   /* memset, strncpy, strlen, strncmp */
22	#include <stdint.h>

24	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
25	 * Internal helpers
26	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
27	
28	/* fnv1a_32 — FNV-1a 32-bit hash over a NUL-terminated string. */
29	static uint32_t fnv1a_32(const char *s)
30	{
31	    uint32_t hash = 2166136261U; /* FNV offset basis */
32	    uint32_t i;
33	
34	    assert(s != NULL);
35	
36	    for (i = 0U; i < ATOM_MAX_LEN + 1U && s[i] != '\0'; ++i) {
37	        hash ^= (uint32_t)(unsigned char)s[i];
38	        hash *= 16777619U; /* FNV prime */
39	    }
40	    return hash;
41	}
42	
43	/*
44	 * probe_slot — linear-probe search.
45	 * Returns the index of the matching slot or the first empty slot.
46	 * *found is set to 1 if the atom already exists, 0 otherwise.
47	 * Returns ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY when the table is full with no match.
48	 */
49	static uint32_t probe_slot(const AtomTable *t, const char *spelling,
50	                            uint32_t hash, int *found)
51	{
52	    uint32_t idx  = hash % ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY;
53	    uint32_t step = 0U;
54	
55	    assert(t       != NULL);
56	    assert(spelling != NULL);
57	    assert(found   != NULL);
58	
59	    *found = 0;
60	
61	    for (step = 0U; step < ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY; ++step) {
62	        const Atom *slot = &t->slots[idx];
63	
64	        if (slot->id == ATOM_ID_INVALID) {
65	            return idx; /* empty — can insert here */
66	        }
67	
68	        if (slot->hash == hash &&
69	            strncmp(slot->spelling, spelling, ATOM_MAX_LEN) == 0) {
70	            *found = 1;
71	            return idx; /* existing match */
72	        }
73	
74	        idx = (idx + 1U) % ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY;
75	    }
76	
77	    return ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY; /* table full, no match */
78	}
79	
80	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	 * Public API
82	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
83	
84	int atom_table_init(AtomTable *t)
85	{
86	    if (t == NULL) {
87	        return -1;
88	    }
89	    memset(t, 0, sizeof(AtomTable));
90	    return 0;
91	}
92	
93	AtomId atom_intern(AtomTable *t, const char *spelling)
94	{
95	    uint32_t hash;
96	    uint32_t idx;
97	    int      found;
98	    size_t   len;
99	    Atom    *slot;
100	
101	    if (t == NULL || spelling == NULL) {
102	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
103	    }
104	
105	    len = strnlen(spelling, ATOM_MAX_LEN + 1U);
106	    if (len > ATOM_MAX_LEN) {
107	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
108	    }
109	
110	    hash = fnv1a_32(spelling);
111	    idx  = probe_slot(t, spelling, hash, &found);
112	
113	    if (idx == ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY) {
114	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID; /* table full */
115	    }
116	
117	    if (found) {
118	        return t->slots[idx].id;
119	    }
120	
121	    /* Insert new atom. */
122	    assert(t->count < ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY);
123	
124	    slot = &t->slots[idx];
125	    /* memcpy + explicit NUL — avoids MSVC strncpy deprecation warning. */
126	    memcpy(slot->spelling, spelling, len);
127	    slot->spelling[len] = '\0';
128	    slot->hash = hash;
129	    slot->id   = (AtomId)(t->count + ATOM_ID_MIN);
130	
131	    t->count++;
132	    return slot->id;
133	}
134	
135	AtomId atom_lookup(const AtomTable *t, const char *spelling)
136	{
137	    uint32_t hash;
138	    uint32_t idx;
139	    int      found;
140	    size_t   len;
141	
142	    if (t == NULL || spelling == NULL) {
143	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
144	    }
145	
146	    len = strnlen(spelling, ATOM_MAX_LEN + 1U);
147	    if (len > ATOM_MAX_LEN) {
148	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
149	    }
150	
151	    hash = fnv1a_32(spelling);
152	    idx  = probe_slot(t, spelling, hash, &found);
153	
154	    if (!found || idx == ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY) {
155	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
156	    }
157	
158	    return t->slots[idx].id;
159	}
160	
161	const char *atom_spelling(const AtomTable *t, AtomId id)
162	{
163	    uint32_t slot_index;
164	    uint32_t i;
165	
166	    if (t == NULL || id == ATOM_ID_INVALID) {
167	        return NULL;
168	    }
169	
170	    /*
171	     * Linear scan to find the slot whose id matches.
172	     * This path is not performance-critical (used for display / debug).
173	     * Bounded by ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY (JPL Rule 2).
174	     */
175	    for (i = 0U; i < ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY; ++i) {
176	        if (t->slots[i].id == id) {
177	            return t->slots[i].spelling;
178	        }
179	    }
180	
181	    (void)slot_index; /* suppressed: unused after refactor */
182	    return NULL;
183	}
184	
185	uint32_t atom_count(const AtomTable *t)
186	{
187	    if (t == NULL) {
188	        return 0U;
189	    }
190	    return t->count;
191	}

2	 * atoms.h — Atom table for the Epilog inference engine.
3	 *
4	 * An atom is an immutable, interned string. Every unique spelling maps to
5	 * exactly one AtomId. Comparisons are therefore O(1) integer comparisons.
6	 *
7	 * JPL rules observed:
8	 *   - No dynamic allocation after atom_table_init().
9	 *   - All loops have a statically provable upper bound (ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY).
10	 *   - No recursion.
11	 *   - No more than one level of pointer indirection in public API.
12	 *   - Every function documents its preconditions; callers must check returns.
13	 */
14	
15	#ifndef EPILOG_ATOMS_H
16	#define EPILOG_ATOMS_H
17	
18	#include <stddef.h>   /* size_t  */
19	#include <stdint.h>   /* uint32_t */
20	
21	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
22	 * Compile-time limits (Rule 2: fixed upper bounds for all loops/tables).
23	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
24	
25	#define ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY  4096U   /* max distinct atoms     */
26	#define ATOM_MAX_LEN          255U   /* max chars, excl. NUL   */
27	
28	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	 * Public types
30	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
31	
32	/*
33	 * AtomId — opaque handle; ATOM_ID_INVALID signals absence / error.
34	 * Zero is intentionally reserved so zero-initialised structs are safe.
35	 */
36	typedef uint32_t AtomId;
37	#define ATOM_ID_INVALID  0U
38	#define ATOM_ID_MIN      1U
39	
40	/* Internal storage for one interned atom. */
41	typedef struct {
42	    char     spelling[ATOM_MAX_LEN + 1U]; /* NUL-terminated              */
43	    uint32_t hash;                         /* pre-computed FNV-1a hash    */
44	    AtomId   id;                           /* == slot index + ATOM_ID_MIN */
45	} Atom;
46

49	 * Allocate on the stack or as a module-level static; do NOT heap-alloc.
50	 */
51	typedef struct {

53	    uint32_t count;   /* number of interned atoms */
54	} AtomTable;

65	int atom_table_init(AtomTable *t);

71	 * spelling must not be NULL.

[140] [tool_result]  RESULT: 1	/*
2	 * variables.h — Logic variable registry for the Epilog inference engine.
3	 *
4	 * A logic variable is an unbound or bound slot in a unification frame.
5	 * Variables are identified by a VarId scoped to a VarRegistry that lives
6	 * for the duration of a single query. The registry is reset between queries;
7	 * no heap allocation occurs after init.
8	 *
9	 * Binding is represented as a union-find structure without path compression
10	 * to keep pointer depth ≤ 1 and behaviour fully predictable (JPL rule 7).
11	 * Binding chains are therefore at most VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY long, which is
12	 * statically bounded (JPL rule 2).
13	 *
14	 * JPL rules observed:
15	 *   - No dynamic allocation after var_registry_init().
16	 *   - All loops have a statically provable upper bound.
17	 *   - No recursion — walk() is an explicit bounded loop.
18	 *   - No more than one level of pointer indirection in public API.
19	 *   - Every function checks its parameters; callers must check returns.
20	 */
21	
22	#ifndef EPILOG_VARIABLES_H
23	#define EPILOG_VARIABLES_H
24	
25	#include <stddef.h>    /* size_t   */
26	#include <stdint.h>    /* uint32_t */
27	#include "atoms.h"     /* AtomId   */
28	
29	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	 * Compile-time limits
31	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
32	
33	#define VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY  1024U  /* max variables per query frame */
34	#define VAR_NAME_MAX_LEN         63U  /* max chars in a variable name  */
35	
36	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
37	 * Public types
38	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
39	
40	/*
41	 * VarId — opaque handle. VAR_ID_INVALID signals absence / error.
42	 */
43	typedef uint32_t VarId;
44	#define VAR_ID_INVALID  0U
45	#define VAR_ID_MIN      1U
46	
47	/*
48	 * TermTag — discriminates what a bound variable holds.
49	 */
50	typedef enum {
51	    TERM_UNBOUND = 0, /* variable is free          */
52	    TERM_ATOM,        /* bound to an interned atom  */
53	    TERM_VAR          /* bound to another variable  */
54	} TermTag;
55	
56	/*
57	 * Binding — the value slot inside a VarEntry.
58	 * Union kept flat so pointer depth never exceeds 1.
59	 */
60	typedef union {
61	    AtomId atom_id; /* valid when tag == TERM_ATOM */
62	    VarId  var_id;  /* valid when tag == TERM_VAR  */
63	} BindingValue;
64	
65	/*
66	 * VarEntry — one slot in the registry.
67	 */
68	typedef struct {
69	    char         name[VAR_NAME_MAX_LEN + 1U]; /* source-level name, may be "_" */
70	    TermTag      tag;
71	    BindingValue value;
72	    VarId        id; /* == slot index + VAR_ID_MIN */
73	} VarEntry;
74	
75	/*
76	 * VarRegistry — fixed-size store for one query's variables.
77	 * Allocate as a local or static; do NOT heap-alloc.
78	 */
79	typedef struct {
80	    VarEntry entries[VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY];
81	    uint32_t count;
82	} VarRegistry;
83	
84	/*
85	 * WalkResult — return type for var_walk.
86	 */

88	    TermTag      tag;
89	    BindingValue value;    /* meaningful when tag != TERM_UNBOUND */
90	    VarId        root_id;  /* the canonical (deepest bound) VarId */
91	} WalkResult;
92

95	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
96

99	 * Must be called once per query, before any other var_* function.
100	 * Returns 0 on success, -1 if r is NULL.
101	 */
102	int var_registry_init(VarRegistry *r);
103	
104	/*
105	 * var_alloc — allocate a fresh unbound variable named *name.
106	 * name must be NUL-terminated and ≤ VAR_NAME_MAX_LEN chars.
107	 * Returns VAR_ID_INVALID if the registry is full or name is NULL.
108	 */
109	VarId var_alloc(VarRegistry *r, const char *name);
110

116	int var_bind_atom(VarRegistry *r, VarId id, AtomId atom_id);

120	 * Fails (returns -1) if id is already bound or either id is invalid.
121	 * Returns 0 on success.
122	 */
123	int var_bind_var(VarRegistry *r, VarId id, VarId other_id);
124

127	 * Terminates in at most VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY steps (bounded loop, no
128	 * recursion). Returns a WalkResult describing the final state.
129	 * On invalid id, result.tag == TERM_UNBOUND and result.root_id == VAR_ID_INVALID.
130	 */
131	WalkResult var_walk(const VarRegistry *r, VarId id);

2	 * variables.c — Logic variable registry for the Epilog inference engine.

4	 * Variables are allocated per-query from a fixed-size VarRegistry.
5	 * Binding chains are walked with an explicit bounded loop (no recursion).
6	 * No heap allocation occurs after var_registry_init().

11	 *   Rule 3  — no dynamic memory allocation after var_registry_init().

13	 *   Rule 5  — every parameter validated; every return value is meaningful.
14	 *   Rule 6  — preprocessor used only for include and simple constants.

16	 *   Rule 8  — compiled with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic.

28	/*
29	 * entry_at — bounds-checked slot accessor.
30	 * Returns NULL when id is out of range; avoids pointer arithmetic elsewhere.
31	 */
32	static VarEntry *entry_at(VarRegistry *r, VarId id)
33	{
34	    uint32_t idx;
35	
36	    assert(r != NULL);
37	
38	    if (id == VAR_ID_INVALID || id < VAR_ID_MIN) {
39	        return NULL;
40	    }
41	
42	    idx = id - VAR_ID_MIN;
43	
44	    if (idx >= VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY || idx >= r->count) {
45	        return NULL;
46	    }
47	
48	    return &r->entries[idx];
49	}
50	
51	/* const variant for read-only callers */
52	static const VarEntry *entry_at_c(const VarRegistry *r, VarId id)
53	{
54	    uint32_t idx;
55	
56	    assert(r != NULL);
57	
58	    if (id == VAR_ID_INVALID || id < VAR_ID_MIN) {
59	        return NULL;
60	    }
61	
62	    idx = id - VAR_ID_MIN;
63	
64	    if (idx >= VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY || idx >= r->count) {
65	        return NULL;
66	    }
67	
68	    return &r->entries[idx];
69	}

75	int var_registry_init(VarRegistry *r)
76	{
77	    if (r == NULL) {
78	        return -1;
79	    }
80	    memset(r, 0, sizeof(VarRegistry));
81	    return 0;
82	}
83	
84	VarId var_alloc(VarRegistry *r, const char *name)
85	{
86	    VarEntry *slot;
87	    size_t    len;
88	    VarId     new_id;
89	
90	    if (r == NULL || name == NULL) {
91	        return VAR_ID_INVALID;
92	    }
93	
94	    if (r->count >= VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY) {
95	        return VAR_ID_INVALID;
96	    }
97	
98	    len = strnlen(name, VAR_NAME_MAX_LEN + 1U);
99	    if (len > VAR_NAME_MAX_LEN) {
100	        return VAR_ID_INVALID;
101	    }
102	
103	    new_id = (VarId)(r->count + VAR_ID_MIN);
104	    slot   = &r->entries[r->count];
105	
106	    memset(slot, 0, sizeof(VarEntry));
107	    memcpy(slot->name, name, len);
108	    slot->name[len] = '\0';
109	    slot->tag       = TERM_UNBOUND;
110	    slot->id        = new_id;
111	
112	    r->count++;
113	    return new_id;
114	}
115	
116	int var_bind_atom(VarRegistry *r, VarId id, AtomId atom_id)
117	{
118	    VarEntry *e;
119	
120	    if (r == NULL || atom_id == ATOM_ID_INVALID) {
121	        return -1;
122	    }
123	
124	    e = entry_at(r, id);
125	    if (e == NULL) {
126	        return -1;
127	    }
128	
129	    if (e->tag != TERM_UNBOUND) {
130	        return -1; /* already bound */
131	    }
132	
133	    e->tag         = TERM_ATOM;
134	    e->value.atom_id = atom_id;
135	    return 0;
136	}
137	
138	int var_bind_var(VarRegistry *r, VarId id, VarId other_id)
139	{
140	    VarEntry *e;
141	
142	    if (r == NULL) {
143	        return -1;
144	    }
145	
146	    /* Binding a variable to itself is a no-op, not an error. */
147	    if (id == other_id) {
148	        return 0;
149	    }
150	
151	    e = entry_at(r, id);
152	    if (e == NULL) {
153	        return -1;
154	    }
155	
156	    if (entry_at(r, other_id) == NULL) {
157	        return -1; /* other_id doesn't exist */
158	    }
159	
160	    if (e->tag != TERM_UNBOUND) {
161	        return -1; /* already bound */
162	    }
163	
164	    e->tag          = TERM_VAR;
165	    e->value.var_id = other_id;
166	    return 0;
167	}
168	
169	WalkResult var_walk(const VarRegistry *r, VarId id)
170	{
171	    WalkResult     result;
172	    const VarEntry *e;
173	    VarId           current;
174	    uint32_t        steps;
175	
176	    result.tag            = TERM_UNBOUND;
177	    result.value.var_id   = VAR_ID_INVALID;
178	    result.root_id        = VAR_ID_INVALID;
179	
180	    if (r == NULL || id == VAR_ID_INVALID) {
181	        return result;
182	    }
183	
184	    current = id;
185	
186	    /*
187	     * Follow the binding chain. Bounded by VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY so the
188	     * loop is statically provable to terminate (JPL Rule 2).
189	     * No path compression — keeps pointer depth ≤ 1 (JPL Rule 7).
190	     */
191	    for (steps = 0U; steps < VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY; ++steps) {
192	        e = entry_at_c(r, current);
193	        if (e == NULL) {
194	            return result; /* dangling id — return invalid */
195	        }
196	
197	        if (e->tag != TERM_VAR) {
198	            /* Reached an atom binding or an unbound variable — done. */
199	            result.tag      = e->tag;
200	            result.value    = e->value;
201	            result.root_id  = current;
202	            return result;
203	        }
204	
205	        current = e->value.var_id;
206	    }
207	
208	    /* Should be unreachable: cycle would require more entries than capacity. */
209	    assert(0);
210	    return result;
211	}
212	
213	int var_reset(VarRegistry *r)
214	{
215	    if (r == NULL) {
216	        return -1;
217	    }
218	    memset(r, 0, sizeof(VarRegistry));
219	    return 0;
220	}
221	
222	uint32_t var_count(const VarRegistry *r)
223	{
224	    if (r == NULL) {
225	        return 0U;
226	    }
227	    return r->count;
228	}

[300] [assistant_text] The REPL is running but returning false on the grandparent query. [313] [tool_result]  RESULT: The file d:\Epilog\repl.c has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)
[316] [tool_result]  RESULT: 162	
163	static int load_clauses(ReplState *s, const char *src, const char *label)
164	{
165	    static TokenList tokens; /* 128 KB — too large for stack */
166	    Parser       parser;
167	    ParsedClause clause;
168	    ParseResult  pr;
169	    int          loaded = 0;
170	
171	    memset(&tokens, 0, sizeof(tokens));
172	
173	    if (lex(src, &tokens) < 0) {
174	        fprintf(stderr, "%s: lex error\n", label);
175	        return -1;
176	    }
177	
178	    term_arena_init(&s->arena);
179	    var_registry_init(&s->vars);
180	
181	    if (parser_init(&parser, &tokens, &s->arena, &s->atoms, &s->vars) < 0) {
182	        return -1;
183	    }
184	
185	    for (;;) {
186	        memset(&clause, 0, sizeof(ParsedClause));
187	        pr = parser_next_clause(&parser, &clause);
188	        if (pr == PARSE_EOF) { break; }
189	        if (pr != PARSE_OK) {
190	            fprintf(stderr, "%s: parse error: %s\n", label, parser.error_msg);
191	            return -1;
192	        }
193	        if (db_assert_last(&s->db, &clause, &s->arena) < 0) {
194	            fprintf(stderr, "%s: database full\n", label);
195	            return -1;
196	        }
197	        loaded++;
198	    }
199	    return loaded;
200	}

169	WalkResult var_walk(const VarRegistry *r, VarId id)
170	{
171	    WalkResult     result;
172	    const VarEntry *e;
173	    VarId           current;
174	    uint32_t        steps;
175	
176	    result.tag            = TERM_UNBOUND;
177	    result.value.var_id   = VAR_ID_INVALID;
178	    result.root_id        = VAR_ID_INVALID;
179	
180	    if (r == NULL || id == VAR_ID_INVALID) {
181	        return result;
182	    }
183	
184	    current = id;
185	
186	    /*
187	     * Follow the binding chain. Bounded by VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY so the
188	     * loop is statically provable to terminate (JPL Rule 2).
189	     * No path compression — keeps pointer depth ≤ 1 (JPL Rule 7).
190	     */
191	    for (steps = 0U; steps < VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY; ++steps) {
192	        e = entry_at_c(r, current);
193	        if (e == NULL) {
194	            return result; /* dangling id — return invalid */
195	        }
196	
197	        if (e->tag != TERM_VAR) {
198	            /* Reached an atom binding or an unbound variable — done. */
199	            result.tag      = e->tag;
200	            result.value    = e->value;
201	            result.root_id  = current;
202	            return result;
203	        }
204	
205	        current = e->value.var_id;
206	    }
207	
208	    /* Should be unreachable: cycle would require more entries than capacity. */
209	    assert(0);
210	    return result;
211	}

2	 * solver.c — Backtracking SLD resolution engine.
3	 *
4	 * Execution is iterative over an explicit goal stack and choice-point stack.
5	 * No C-stack recursion (JPL Rule 1). All stacks are bounded (JPL Rule 2).
6	 *
7	 * Algorithm per iteration:
8	 *   1. Pop the top goal.
9	 *   2. Deref it to find functor/arity.
10	 *   3. If it is a built-in, dispatch and handle result.
11	 *   4. Otherwise, look up matching clauses in the database.
12	 *   5. If multiple clauses match, push a ChoicePoint for all but the first.
13	 *   6. Unify goal with clause head; push body goals (reversed) onto goal stack.
14	 *   7. On failure, pop the most recent ChoicePoint and restore state.
15	 *
16	 * Variable scoping: each clause application must use fresh variables.
17	 * We achieve this by copying clause terms into a per-application TermArena
18	 * region and renaming variables — implemented as a "variant" step that
19	 * allocates new VarIds for each clause body instantiation.
20	 */

111	    if (t->kind == TOK_CUT) {
112	        advance(p);
113	        aid = atom_intern(p->atoms, "!");
114	        if (aid == ATOM_ID_INVALID) { return TERM_REF_INVALID; }
115	        return term_make_atom(p->arena, aid);
116	    }
117	
118	    /* atom or compound */
119	    if (t->kind == TOK_ATOM || t->kind == TOK_OP) {
120	        const char *name = t->text;
121	        advance(p);
122	        aid = atom_intern(p->atoms, name);
123	        if (aid == ATOM_ID_INVALID) {
124	            snprintf(p->error_msg, sizeof(p->error_msg),
125	                     "line %u: atom table full", t->line);
126	            return TERM_REF_INVALID;
127	        }
128	
129	        /* compound: atom immediately followed by '(' */
130	        if (peek(p)->kind == TOK_LPAREN) {
131	            TermRef args[TERM_MAX_ARITY];
132	            uint8_t arity = 0U;
133	
134	            advance(p); /* consume '(' */
135	
136	            if (peek(p)->kind != TOK_RPAREN) {
137	                /* parse comma-separated arg list */
138	                uint32_t a;
139	                for (a = 0U; a < (uint32_t)TERM_MAX_ARITY; ++a) {
140	                    TermRef arg = parse_term(p);
141	                    if (arg == TERM_REF_INVALID) { return TERM_REF_INVALID; }
142	                    args[arity++] = arg;
143	                    if (peek(p)->kind != TOK_COMMA) { break; }
144	                    advance(p); /* consume ',' */
145	                }
146	            }
147	
148	            if (expect(p, TOK_RPAREN) == NULL) { return TERM_REF_INVALID; }
149	            ref = term_make_compound(p->arena, aid, arity, args);
150	        } else {
151	            ref = term_make_atom(p->arena, aid);
152	        }
153	
154	        /* infix operator: = or \= immediately following */
155	        {
156	            const Token *op = peek(p);
157	            if (op->kind == TOK_OP &&
158	                (strncmp(op->text, "=",  2) == 0 ||
159	                 strncmp(op->text, "\\=", 3) == 0)) {
160	                char op_name[TOKEN_TEXT_MAX + 1U];
161	                AtomId op_aid;
162	                TermRef rhs;
163	                TermRef pair[2];
164	
165	                memcpy(op_name, op->text, TOKEN_TEXT_MAX);
166	                op_name[TOKEN_TEXT_MAX] = '\0';
167	                advance(p);
168	
169	                rhs = parse_term(p);
170	                if (rhs == TERM_REF_INVALID) { return TERM_REF_INVALID; }
171	
172	                op_aid = atom_intern(p->atoms, op_name);
173	                if (op_aid == ATOM_ID_INVALID) { return TERM_REF_INVALID; }
174	
175	                pair[0] = ref;
176	                pair[1] = rhs;
177	                ref = term_make_compound(p->arena, op_aid, 2U, pair);
178	            }
179	        }
180	
181	        return ref;
182	    }
183	
184	    snprintf(p->error_msg, sizeof(p->error_msg),
185	             "line %u: unexpected token %s '%s'",
186	             t->line, tok_kind_name(t->kind), t->text);
187	    return TERM_REF_INVALID;
188	}

2	 * variables.h — Logic variable registry for the Epilog inference engine.
3	 *
4	 * A logic variable is an unbound or bound slot in a unification frame.
5	 * Variables are identified by a VarId scoped to a VarRegistry that lives
6	 * for the duration of a single query. The registry is reset between queries;
7	 * no heap allocation occurs after init.
8	 *
9	 * Binding is represented as a union-find structure without path compression
10	 * to keep pointer depth ≤ 1 and behaviour fully predictable (JPL rule 7).
11	 * Binding chains are therefore at most VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY long, which is
12	 * statically bounded (JPL rule 2).
13	 *
14	 * JPL rules observed:
15	 *   - No dynamic allocation after var_registry_init().
16	 *   - All loops have a statically provable upper bound.
17	 *   - No recursion — walk() is an explicit bounded loop.
18	 *   - No more than one level of pointer indirection in public API.
19	 *   - Every function checks its parameters; callers must check returns.
20	 */

[687] [tool_result]  RESULT: 1	/*
2	 * terms.h — Term representation for the Epilog inference engine.
3	 *
4	 * A Term is the universal data type of logic programming:
5	 *   - Atom       : an interned string constant  (e.g. alice, foo, [])
6	 *   - Var        : a logic variable             (e.g. X, _G42)
7	 *   - Compound   : a functor + fixed arity args (e.g. parent(alice,bob))
8	 *   - Int        : a machine integer            (e.g. 42)
9	 *
10	 * Storage strategy — no heap after init (JPL Rule 3):
11	 *   All terms live in a TermArena whose backing array is stack- or
12	 *   statically-allocated.  A TermRef is a 32-bit index into that arena.
13	 *   Compound arguments are stored as a contiguous run of TermRefs beginning
14	 *   at arg_start inside a shared ArgPool.
15	 *
16	 * JPL rules observed:
17	 *   Rule 1  — no goto, no recursion.
18	 *   Rule 2  — all loops and capacities statically bounded.
19	 *   Rule 3  — no malloc/free after arena init.
20	 *   Rule 5  — every function validates parameters, returns error codes.
21	 *   Rule 6  — preprocessor limited to includes + constants.
22	 *   Rule 7  — pointer depth ≤ 1 in public API.
23	 */
24

26	#define EPILOG_TERMS_H

2	 * parser.h — Clause and query parser for Epilog.
3	 *

[702] [tool_result]  RESULT: 1	/*
2	 * solver.h — Backtracking resolution engine for Epilog.
3	 *
4	 * The solver executes a list of goals against a Database using SLD resolution.
5	 * It is depth-first and left-to-right, matching standard Prolog semantics.
6	 *
7	 * Execution model:
8	 *   - A ChoicePoint records the state at each point where multiple clauses
9	 *     could match, so backtracking can restore and try the next clause.
10	 *   - The goal stack holds remaining goals for the current branch.
11	 *   - No recursion: the main loop pops goals and pushes new ones iteratively.
12	 *
13	 * The solver calls a SolutionCallback for each solution found.  The callback
14	 * returns SOLVE_NEXT to request more solutions or SOLVE_STOP to halt search.
15	 *
16	 * JPL rules: no recursion, bounded stacks, no post-init malloc.
17	 */
18	
19	#ifndef EPILOG_SOLVER_H
20	#define EPILOG_SOLVER_H

26	#include "database.h"
27	#include "atoms.h"
28	
29	#define GOAL_STACK_CAPACITY    512U
30	#define CHOICE_STACK_CAPACITY  256U
31	#define SOLVE_VAR_BLOCK       1024U  /* vars allocated per frame copy  */
32	
33	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	 * SolveSignal — callback return value.
35	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
36	
37	typedef enum {
38	    SOLVE_NEXT = 0,  /* continue search, yield more solutions */
39	    SOLVE_STOP = 1   /* halt search after this solution       */
40	} SolveSignal;
41

43	 * SolverEnv — everything the solver needs, passed by pointer.
44	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
45	
46	typedef struct {
47	    TermArena   *arena;         /* query-scoped arena (working terms)      */
48	    TermArena   *clause_arena;  /* persistent arena (stored clause terms)  */
49	    VarRegistry *vars;          /* query-scoped variable registry          */
50	    VarRegistry *clause_vars;   /* persistent clause variable registry     */
51	    Trail        trail;
52	    AtomTable   *atoms;

54	} SolverEnv;

58	 *
59	 * Called once per solution. env carries the current (bound) state.

62	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
63

2	 * atoms.c — Atom table implementation for the Epilog inference engine.
3	 *
4	 * Strategy: open-addressed hash table with linear probing.
5	 * All storage is pre-allocated in AtomTable (no malloc after init).
6	 *
7	 * JPL rules observed:
8	 *   Rule 1  — no goto, no setjmp/longjmp, no recursion.
9	 *   Rule 2  — every loop has a fixed upper bound (ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY).
10	 *   Rule 3  — no dynamic memory allocation after atom_table_init().
11	 *   Rule 4  — no function exceeds ~60 lines.
12	 *   Rule 5  — every parameter validated; every return value is meaningful.
13	 *   Rule 6  — preprocessor used only for include and simple constants.
14	 *   Rule 7  — pointer depth ≤ 1 in all operations.
15	 *   Rule 8  — compiled with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic.
16	 */
17

21	#include <string.h>   /* memset, strncpy, strlen, strncmp */

23	
24	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
25	 * Internal helpers
26	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
27	
28	/* fnv1a_32 — FNV-1a 32-bit hash over a NUL-terminated string. */
29	static uint32_t fnv1a_32(const char *s)
30	{
31	    uint32_t hash = 2166136261U; /* FNV offset basis */
32	    uint32_t i;
33	
34	    assert(s != NULL);
35	
36	    for (i = 0U; i < ATOM_MAX_LEN + 1U && s[i] != '\0'; ++i) {
37	        hash ^= (uint32_t)(unsigned char)s[i];
38	        hash *= 16777619U; /* FNV prime */
39	    }
40	    return hash;
41	}
42	
43	/*
44	 * probe_slot — linear-probe search.
45	 * Returns the index of the matching slot or the first empty slot.
46	 * *found is set to 1 if the atom already exists, 0 otherwise.
47	 * Returns ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY when the table is full with no match.
48	 */
49	static uint32_t probe_slot(const AtomTable *t, const char *spelling,
50	                            uint32_t hash, int *found)
51	{
52	    uint32_t idx  = hash % ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY;
53	    uint32_t step = 0U;
54	
55	    assert(t       != NULL);
56	    assert(spelling != NULL);
57	    assert(found   != NULL);
58	
59	    *found = 0;
60	
61	    for (step = 0U; step < ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY; ++step) {
62	        const Atom *slot = &t->slots[idx];
63	
64	        if (slot->id == ATOM_ID_INVALID) {
65	            return idx; /* empty — can insert here */
66	        }
67	
68	        if (slot->hash == hash &&
69	            strncmp(slot->spelling, spelling, ATOM_MAX_LEN) == 0) {
70	            *found = 1;
71	            return idx; /* existing match */
72	        }
73	
74	        idx = (idx + 1U) % ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY;
75	    }
76	
77	    return ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY; /* table full, no match */
78	}
79

85	{

87	        return -1;
88	    }

90	    return 0;

93	AtomId atom_intern(AtomTable *t, const char *spelling)
94	{
95	    uint32_t hash;
96	    uint32_t idx;
97	    int      found;
98	    size_t   len;
99	    Atom    *slot;
100	
101	    if (t == NULL || spelling == NULL) {
102	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
103	    }
104	
105	    len = strnlen(spelling, ATOM_MAX_LEN + 1U);
106	    if (len > ATOM_MAX_LEN) {
107	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
108	    }
109	
110	    hash = fnv1a_32(spelling);
111	    idx  = probe_slot(t, spelling, hash, &found);
112	
113	    if (idx == ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY) {
114	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID; /* table full */
115	    }
116	
117	    if (found) {
118	        return t->slots[idx].id;
119	    }
120	
121	    /* Insert new atom. */
122	    assert(t->count < ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY);
123	
124	    slot = &t->slots[idx];
125	    /* memcpy + explicit NUL — avoids MSVC strncpy deprecation warning. */
126	    memcpy(slot->spelling, spelling, len);
127	    slot->spelling[len] = '\0';
128	    slot->hash = hash;
129	    slot->id   = (AtomId)(t->count + ATOM_ID_MIN);
130	
131	    t->count++;
132	    return slot->id;
133	}
134	
135	AtomId atom_lookup(const AtomTable *t, const char *spelling)
136	{
137	    uint32_t hash;
138	    uint32_t idx;
139	    int      found;
140	    size_t   len;
141	
142	    if (t == NULL || spelling == NULL) {
143	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
144	    }
145	
146	    len = strnlen(spelling, ATOM_MAX_LEN + 1U);
147	    if (len > ATOM_MAX_LEN) {
148	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
149	    }
150	
151	    hash = fnv1a_32(spelling);
152	    idx  = probe_slot(t, spelling, hash, &found);
153	
154	    if (!found || idx == ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY) {
155	        return ATOM_ID_INVALID;
156	    }
157	
158	    return t->slots[idx].id;
159	}
160	
161	const char *atom_spelling(const AtomTable *t, AtomId id)
162	{
163	    uint32_t slot_index;
164	    uint32_t i;
165	
166	    if (t == NULL || id == ATOM_ID_INVALID) {
167	        return NULL;
168	    }
169	
170	    /*
171	     * Linear scan to find the slot whose id matches.
172	     * This path is not performance-critical (used for display / debug).
173	     * Bounded by ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY (JPL Rule 2).
174	     */
175	    for (i = 0U; i < ATOM_TABLE_CAPACITY; ++i) {
176	        if (t->slots[i].id == id) {
177	            return t->slots[i].spelling;
178	        }
179	    }
180	
181	    (void)slot_index; /* suppressed: unused after refactor */
182	    return NULL;
183	}

188	        return 0U;
189	    }
190	    return t->count;

184	WalkResult var_walk(const VarRegistry *r, VarId id)
185	{
186	    WalkResult     result;
187	    const VarEntry *e;
188	    VarId           current;
189	    uint32_t        steps;
190	
191	    result.tag            = TERM_UNBOUND;
192	    result.value.var_id   = VAR_ID_INVALID;
193	    result.root_id        = VAR_ID_INVALID;
194	
195	    if (r == NULL || id == VAR_ID_INVALID) {
196	        return result;
197	    }
198	
199	    current = id;
200	
201	    /*
202	     * Follow the binding chain. Bounded by VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY so the
203	     * loop is statically provable to terminate (JPL Rule 2).
204	     * No path compression — keeps pointer depth ≤ 1 (JPL Rule 7).
205	     */
206	    for (steps = 0U; steps < VAR_REGISTRY_CAPACITY; ++steps) {
207	        e = entry_at_c(r, current);
208	        if (e == NULL) {
209	            return result; /* dangling id — return invalid */
210	        }
211	
212	        if (e->tag != TERM_VAR) {
213	            /* Reached an atom binding or an unbound variable — done. */
214	            result.tag      = e->tag;
215	            result.value    = e->value;
216	            result.root_id  = current;
217	            return result;
218	        }
219	
220	        current = e->value.var_id;
221	    }
222	
223	    /* Should be unreachable: cycle would require more entries than capacity. */
224	    assert(0);
225	    return result;
226	}

2	 * lexer.c — Tokenizer implementation.

17	static int is_alpha(char c)  { return (c>='a'&&c<='z')||(c>='A'&&c<='Z'); }
18	static int is_digit(char c)  { return c>='0' && c<='9'; }
19	static int is_lower(char c)  { return c>='a' && c<='z'; }
20	static int is_upper(char c)  { return c>='A' && c<='Z'; }
21	static int is_alnum(char c)  { return is_alpha(c) || is_digit(c) || c=='_'; }
22	static int is_space(char c)  { return c==' '||c=='\t'||c=='\r'||c=='\n'; }
23	
24	static int is_op_char(char c)
25	{
26	    return c=='='||c=='\\'||c=='+'||c=='-'||c=='*'||c=='/'||
27	           c=='<'||c=='>'||c=='@'||c=='#'||c=='^'||c=='~';
28	}

30	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	 * append_token — add one token to the list; returns 0 or -1 on overflow.
32	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
33	
34	static int append_token(TokenList *out, TokenKind kind,
35	                        const char *text, int32_t int_val, uint32_t line)
36	{
37	    Token *t;
38	
39	    assert(out != NULL);
40	
41	    if (out->count >= TOKEN_LIST_CAPACITY) {
42	        return -1;
43	    }
44	
45	    t = &out->items[out->count];
46	    t->kind    = kind;
47	    t->int_val = int_val;
48	    t->line    = line;
49	
50	    if (text != NULL) {
51	        size_t len = strnlen(text, TOKEN_TEXT_MAX);
52	        memcpy(t->text, text, len);
53	        t->text[len] = '\0';
54	    } else {
55	        t->text[0] = '\0';
56	    }
57	
58	    out->count++;
59	    return 0;
60	}

62	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
63	 * lex
64	 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
65	
66	int lex(const char *src, TokenList *out)
67	{
68	    uint32_t i;
69	    uint32_t len;
70	    uint32_t line;
71	    char     buf[TOKEN_TEXT_MAX + 1U];
72	    uint32_t buf_pos;
73	
74	    if (src == NULL || out == NULL) {
75	        return -1;
76	    }
77	
78	    memset(out, 0, sizeof(TokenList));
79	    len  = (uint32_t)strnlen(src, 1U << 20); /* 1 MB cap */
80	    line = 1U;
81	    i    = 0U;
82	
83	    while (i < len) {
84	        char c = src[i];
85	
86	        /* skip whitespace */
87	        if (is_space(c)) {
88	            if (c == '\n') { line++; }
89	            i++;
90	            continue;
91	        }
92	
93	        /* line comment */
94	        if (c == '%') {
95	            while (i < len && src[i] != '\n') { i++; }
96	            continue;
97	        }
98	
99	        /* block comment */
100	        if (c == '/' && i + 1U < len && src[i + 1U] == '*') {
101	            uint32_t depth = 1U;
102	            i += 2U;
103	            while (i + 1U < len && depth > 0U) {
104	                if (src[i] == '\n')                          { line++; }
105	                if (src[i] == '*' && src[i+1U] == '/')      { depth--; i += 2U; continue; }
106	                if (src[i] == '/' && src[i+1U] == '*')      { depth++; i += 2U; continue; }
107	                i++;
108	            }
109	            continue;
110	        }
111	
112	        /* atom: lowercase-initial or operator-sequence */
113	        if (is_lower(c)) {
114	            buf_pos = 0U;
115	            while (i < len && is_alnum(src[i]) && buf_pos < TOKEN_TEXT_MAX) {
116	                buf[buf_pos++] = src[i++];
117	            }
118	            buf[buf_pos] = '\0';
119	            if (append_token(out, TOK_ATOM, buf, 0, line) < 0) { return -1; }
120	            continue;
121	        }
122	
123	        /* variable: uppercase or underscore initial */
124	        if (is_upper(c) || c == '_') {
125	            buf_pos = 0U;
126	            while (i < len && is_alnum(src[i]) && buf_pos < TOKEN_TEXT_MAX) {
127	                buf[buf_pos++] = src[i++];
128	            }
129	            buf[buf_pos] = '\0';
130	            if (append_token(out, TOK_VAR, buf, 0, line) < 0) { return -1; }
131	            continue;
132	        }
133	
134	        /* integer */
135	        if (is_digit(c)) {
136	            int32_t val = 0;
137	            buf_pos = 0U;
138	            while (i < len && is_digit(src[i]) && buf_pos < TOKEN_TEXT_MAX) {
139	                val = val * 10 + (int32_t)(src[i] - '0');
140	                buf[buf_pos++] = src[i++];
141	            }
142	            buf[buf_pos] = '\0';
143	            if (append_token(out, TOK_INT, buf, val, line) < 0) { return -1; }
144	            continue;
145	        }
146	
147	        /* single-quoted atom */
148	        if (c == '\'') {
149	            buf_pos = 0U;
150	            i++; /* skip opening quote */
151	            while (i < len && src[i] != '\'' && buf_pos < TOKEN_TEXT_MAX) {
152	                if (src[i] == '\n') { line++; }
153	                buf[buf_pos++] = src[i++];
154	            }
155	            if (i < len) { i++; } /* skip closing quote */
156	            buf[buf_pos] = '\0';
157	            if (append_token(out, TOK_ATOM, buf, 0, line) < 0) { return -1; }
158	            continue;
159	        }
160	
161	        /* two-character tokens */
162	        if (c == ':' && i + 1U < len && src[i+1U] == '-') {
163	            if (append_token(out, TOK_NECK,  ":-", 0, line) < 0) { return -1; }
164	            i += 2U; continue;
165	        }
166	        if (c == '?' && i + 1U < len && src[i+1U] == '-') {
167	            if (append_token(out, TOK_QUERY, "?-", 0, line) < 0) { return -1; }
168	            i += 2U; continue;
169	        }
170	        if (c == '\\' && i + 1U < len && src[i+1U] == '=') {
171	            if (append_token(out, TOK_OP,    "\\=", 0, line) < 0) { return -1; }
172	            i += 2U; continue;
173	        }
174	
175	        /* operator sequences (=, etc.) */
176	        if (is_op_char(c)) {
177	            buf_pos = 0U;
178	            while (i < len && is_op_char(src[i]) && buf_pos < TOKEN_TEXT_MAX) {
179	                buf[buf_pos++] = src[i++];
180	            }
181	            buf[buf_pos] = '\0';
182	            if (append_token(out, TOK_OP, buf, 0, line) < 0) { return -1; }
183	            continue;
184	        }
185	
186	        /* single-character punctuation */
187	        switch (c) {
188	            case '(': append_token(out, TOK_LPAREN, "(", 0, line); break;
189	            case ')': append_token(out, TOK_RPAREN, ")", 0, line); break;
190	            case ',': append_token(out, TOK_COMMA,  ",", 0, line); break;
191	            case '.':
192	                /* '.' followed by whitespace or EOF is clause terminator */
193	                if (i + 1U >= len || is_space(src[i+1U])) {
194	                    append_token(out, TOK_DOT, ".", 0, line);
195	                } else {
196	                    append_token(out, TOK_OP, ".", 0, line);
197	                }
198	                break;
199	            case '|': append_token(out, TOK_PIPE,  "|", 0, line); break;
200	            case ';': append_token(out, TOK_SEMI,  ";", 0, line); break;
201	            case '!': append_token(out, TOK_CUT,   "!", 0, line); break;
202	            default: {
203	                char err[2] = { c, '\0' };
204	                append_token(out, TOK_ERROR, err, 0, line);
205	                return -1;
206	            }
207	        }
208	        i++;
209	    }
210	
211	    append_token(out, TOK_EOF, "", 0, line);
212	    return 0;
213	}
214	
215	const char *tok_kind_name(TokenKind k)
216	{
217	    switch (k) {
218	        case TOK_ATOM:   return "atom";
219	        case TOK_VAR:    return "variable";
220	        case TOK_INT:    return "integer";
221	        case TOK_LPAREN: return "'('";
222	        case TOK_RPAREN: return "')'";
223	        case TOK_COMMA:  return "','";
224	        case TOK_DOT:    return "'.'";
225	        case TOK_NECK:   return "':-'";
226	        case TOK_QUERY:  return "'?-'";
227	        case TOK_PIPE:   return "'|'";
228	        case TOK_SEMI:   return "';'";
229	        case TOK_CUT:    return "'!'";
230	        case TOK_OP:     return "operator";
231	        case TOK_EOF:    return "EOF";
232	        case TOK_ERROR:  return "error";
233	        default:         return "unknown";
234	    }
235	}

19	/* peek — return current token without advancing. */
20	static const Token *peek(const Parser *p)
21	{
22	    assert(p != NULL && p->tokens != NULL);
23	    if (p->pos >= p->tokens->count) {
24	        return &p->tokens->items[p->tokens->count - 1U]; /* EOF */
25	    }
26	    return &p->tokens->items[p->pos];
27	}
28	
29	/* advance — consume and return current token. */
30	static const Token *advance(Parser *p)
31	{
32	    const Token *t = peek(p);
33	    if (t->kind != TOK_EOF) { p->pos++; }
34	    return t;
35	}
36	
37	/* expect — consume token of expected kind; returns NULL and sets error otherwise. */
38	static const Token *expect(Parser *p, TokenKind kind)
39	{
40	    const Token *t = peek(p);
41	    if (t->kind != kind) {
42	        snprintf(p->error_msg, sizeof(p->error_msg),
43	                 "line %u: expected %s, got %s '%s'",
44	                 t->line, tok_kind_name(kind), tok_kind_name(t->kind), t->text);
45	        return NULL;
46	    }
47	    return advance(p);
48	}
